Ogun 2027: PDP chieftain denies governorship ambition
items.description: — Alleges misuse of name, calls for INEC investigation By Jimoh Babatunde A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ogun State, Topa Olusegun Peter, has denied reports identifying him as a governorship aspirant for the 2027 election, alleging that his name was used without his consent. Peter, the Baale of Olorunsogo, Ilara, in Imeko-Afon Local Government Area, made the clarification while addressing journalists in Abeokuta on Saturday. He alleged that the All Progressives Congress (APC) chairman in the council, Ramoni Adebolu, and some other APC chieftains had approached him with a political offer before his name appeared in newspaper publications as a PDP governorship aspirant. Peter said he neither purchased a governorship nomination form nor signed any document indicating his intention to contest the election. He also denied authorising anyone to act on his behalf in connection with the purported ambition. According to him, the controversy began when Adebolu and other politicians met him in his hometown of Ilara and informed him that they had a political position to offer him under the PDP. He said he rejected the proposal because he was not interested in the arrangement. “We met in my hometown, Ilara, and they informed me that the position was under the PDP but did not explain its exact nature. But I told them there and then that I was not interested because such could only come from my party, the PDP,” he said. Peter alleged that after his name appeared in newspaper publications, he contacted Adebolu for an explanation. He claimed that the APC chairman urged him to remain calm and promised him financial benefits, a car and a major political appointment if Senator Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, emerged as the APC governorship candidate. The PDP chieftain, however, insisted that he did not collect money from Adebolu or any of the other individuals he mentioned. “For the avoidance of doubt, I did not collect any money from the individuals mentioned in this statement,” he said. Peter also expressed concern over a purported petition reportedly submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) by a lawyer, Anderson Asemota of Neplus Ultra Attorneys, allegedly asking the commission to publish his client’s name as a governorship aspirant within 48 hours. He denied knowing the lawyer or authorising him to write to INEC on his behalf. “I have never spoken with or met the lawyer, Anderson Asemota of Neplus Ultra Attorneys, alleged to have written the petition on my behalf,” he said. Peter called on INEC to investigate the circumstances surrounding the reported correspondence and establish how his name was allegedly used without his knowledge. He also urged the commission to disregard any document purportedly submitted by him or on his behalf until the matter was clarified. “I therefore call for a thorough investigation into how my name came to be used in this manner and how documents were submitted in my name without my knowledge,” he said. The PDP chieftain further appealed to security agencies and other relevant authorities to ensure the safety of himself and his family, saying the circumstances surrounding the controversy had caused him serious concern. Although he did not disclose any specific threat against them, he urged the authorities to investigate the matter and bring anyone found culpable to justice. Peter used the opportunity to reaffirm his loyalty to the PDP, saying he had been a member of the party since its formation in 1998 and had never defected to another political platform. He also said Hon. Ladi Adebutu emerged as the PDP’s sole candidate in the Ogun State governorship primary held on May 24, 2026, an exercise he claimed to have supervised in his ward. He said the development further underscored the need to clarify how he came to be identified as a governorship aspirant. The post Ogun 2027: PDP chieftain denies governorship ambition appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: The Kiss That Cancelled a Wedding Before the Pastor Could Say Amen!
items.description: My people, we have entered dangerous times. A wedding has reportedly collapsed because the bride blew a kiss to her former boyfriend. Not an actual kiss, mind you. A flying kiss! One that travelled through the atmosphere without a passport, visa or boarding pass and, as far as we know, never even landed! Marriage has become a high-risk investment! According to the story accompanying a viral video, the bride spotted her ex near the church and allegedly dispatched a kiss in his direction. The groom, apparently operating a zero-tolerance policy on the importation of affection from previous relationships, reportedly cancelled the wedding immediately. Just like that! Even ECG gives notice sometimes before disconnecting electricity. This gentleman allegedly disconnected an entire marriage before the pastor could say, “Dearly beloved!” Now, before we condemn the groom, let us examine the seriousness of the offence. In matters of love, former boyfriends are supposed to remain in the archives, preferably under lock and key. Unfortunately, some people insist on maintaining diplomatic relations with former territories, even on the day of their presidential inauguration. But was the offence the kiss itself, its destination or the fact that the recipient was an ex? If the bride had blown the same kiss towards her grandmother, would the wedding have continued? And if the ex had ducked, allowing the kiss to land harmlessly on a nearby goat, would the marriage have been saved? These are constitutional questions requiring the intervention of the Supreme Court of Matrimonial Affairs. Meanwhile, Facebook has constituted itself into a Commission of Inquiry. Judges, prosecutors, relationship counsellors and survivors of previous romantic earthquakes have assembled to deliver their verdicts. One gentleman congratulates the groom for escaping a lifetime of trouble. Another wants to know who invited the ex. A third insists the bride was already displaying symptoms of future infidelity. Wonderful! Some people can now diagnose twenty years of marital unfaithfulness from a two-second flying kiss. Even our most celebrated prophets, with all their spiritual surveillance equipment, cannot compete with such extraordinary powers of revelation. But the bride has her defenders too. They argue that the groom overreacted. After all, nobody was physically kissed. There was no bodily contact, no acknowledgement of receipt and certainly no evidence that the ex signed for the consignment. Perhaps the Ghana Civil Aviation Authority should intervene. Henceforth, all kisses directed towards former lovers must obtain flight clearance and maintain a safe distance from matrimonial airspace. Personally, I am more worried about the wedding expenses. Imagine the marriage lists, expensive kente, photographers, caterers, rented chairs and relatives transported from villages where even Google Maps requires directions. All these investments wiped out by a kiss that cost absolutely nothing! Somewhere, an auntie has borrowed money to buy a magnificent outfit, only to discover that the marriage has died before the reception. And what happens to the jollof? Whatever the alleged romantic misconduct, innocent rice must not suffer collective punishment! Of course, beneath the comedy lies a serious matter. Relationships require trust, respect and sensible boundaries. But misunderstandings also deserve conversation before an entire marriage is sentenced to death. Besides, we have only a viral caption and a short video, not the full facts. Yet social media has already convicted the bride, decorated the groom and sentenced the ex without hearing a single witness! In the Republic of Uncommon Sense, we have learnt one important lesson: a kiss no longer needs to touch anybody to destroy a wedding. And please, before blowing your next kiss, check the direction of the wind. You might accidentally blow away your marriage! NOW, LET THE REPUBLIC DECIDE: Was the groom a wise man who escaped disaster, or a man who allowed a kiss that never landed to blow away his marriage?

items.title: Bilawal says KP governor's rule could end if opposition engages with Centre on counterterrorism policy
items.description: PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said on Sunday that if the opposition was willing to fight against terrorism and engage with the Centre on a plan, governor’s rule and emergency imposed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa could end. He made these remarks while speaking to the media in Karachi, where he was visiting the Karsaz Monument on the 19th anniversary of the Karsaz bombing . His statement comes a week after the Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move also followed a mobilisation drive and protest march by the PTI, which was in power in KP and in opposition in the Centre, to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. “If they really want to fight terrorists, and if they want that emergency and governor’s rule in KP to end, they should engage with the federal government and politicians and discuss a united policy regarding the fight against terrorism,” Bilawal said on Sunday, referring to the PTI-led opposition. He added that if the opposition was ready to fight terrorism and “we agree on a plan” to do so, the emergency and governor’s rule in KP could end. “If the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister (Sohail Afridi) is a coward, if he is not ready to defend his homeland, if he is not ready to fight those terrorists, then the PPP is ready to fight them,” Bilawal said. “That is why we supported the government’s decision to impose governor’s rule in KP.” He stressed that the party would “join forces with everyone to fight these terrorists”. In his media talk, the Bhutto scion said the country had reached a point where “terrorist attacks are taking place from Khyber to Khuzdar”. He regretted that when the Taliban came to power in Kabul in 2021, the Pakistani government at that time “also decided to invite the terrorists who were in Afghanistan to come back and live in our Swat, our Malakand, our former tribal areas”. He was seemingly referring to then-prime minister Imran’s plans to resettle members of the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan in the country. Bilawal went on to say that terrorists who were in jail in Pakistan were also freed. “Today, Pakistan is suffering the losses from these wrong decisions,” he lamented. He added that the country had now once again reached the point where “some forces want to take down Pakistan’s flag in Swat” and there was a fight against terrorism ongoing across the entire country, while security forces, law enforcers and the public were being targeted. However, he claimed, in the province where the highest number of terrorist incidents were taking place — KP — its chief minister had pledged that he would not face the terrorists. In response to a question about the Karsaz bombing, the PPP chairman remarked that the greatest loss was caused when terrorist incidents were not taken seriously. He said that the PPP had “prepared entire society” to fight terrorism by creating an environment for counterterrorism operations in 2008, when the party was in power. After that, he said, when the National Action Plan was introduced, the PPP adopted a holistic approach towards bringing changes in institutions to assist with combatting terrorism. He emphasised that success was achieved when “every citizen” of Pakistan joined the fight against terrorism, saying, “Today as well, we will make efforts to create an environment where we are all united, and will fight the terrorists together.” Answering further questions, he said Pakistan was facing a “historic economic crisis”. “It appears that the situation will worsen. Our priority is to address this economic crisis, and to do that, we will have to fight terrorism as well,” he added. He said efforts should also be made to improve the democratic and electoral system in Pakistan. For this reason, he said, the PPP had highlighted the need for a new NAP and consensus on the fight against terrorism, while also extending an invitation to the opposition to play a part in this. He said the PPP also made an effort to improve the democratic system by pushing for electoral reforms. To this end, the federal government had decided to establish an electoral reforms committee in the National Assembly, adding that he had invited the opposition to play their part in that committee as well. “If they say that democracy is weak in this country, they should help us to strengthen it,” the PPP chairman said. He added, “If we can create such an environment, we will be in a better position to fight terrorists.” Bilawal also said KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi had been nominated by the PPP for the office of governor, but “constitutionally, he is now a representative of the federal government”. He said Kundi reported to the federal government, but “I will keep talking to him and keep advising him; in principle, though, he is now working together with the federal government”. Responding to a question regarding a potential “compromise” with the opposition, Bilawal said, “You say ‘compromise’ like it’s a bad word […] Compromise and politics go hand in hand.” He stressed that ex-PM Benazir had always strived for compromises during her political career, adding that she knew that one could reach “extremes” if they remained a revolutionary or an activist who only protested rather than working for their cause. “We had to solve our issues and lift the public and our workers out of difficulty,” Bilawal said about the PPP’s past tenures in government. He asserted that it was the result of the PPP’s “compromises” that led to the end of Gen Pervez Musharraf’s dictatorship, as well as the passage of the 1973 Constitution and the 18th Amendment. “We (the PPP) are not in the federal government. Nor do we have a majority in Parliament,” he said. “But [we have to see] how we can conduct politics in the space we have.” New provinces Answering a question regarding the creation of new provinces, Bilawal stated that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi knew “clearly” what the PPP and President Asif Ali Zardari’s policy was regarding new provinces or administrative units, and that this was “not possible without the president’s signature”. Naqvi’s July remarks calling for new provinces and reforms in the current governance system had ignited an animated debate across the country. The PPP, which rules Sindh, has strongly opposed any possible division of the province. Bilawal stressed that the PPP’s position was clear: that they could be created in accordance with the Constitution and law if the provincial assembly agreed. The Sindh Assembly, amid a boycott by the opposition, adopted a resolution last month rejecting all attempts to divide the province or create new administrative units. “Where there is consensus and it is not a political stunt, if there is no other purpose behind it … why aren’t provinces being made there?” the PPP chairman said, giving the example of Gilgit-Baltistan. “If we really want this to be implemented, it must only be implemented where the provinces want this,” he stressed, noting that the entire GB Legislative Assembly had passed a resolution with consensus for the region’s constitutional rights. Bilawal requested politicians, whether on the treasury or opposition benches, not to politicise the issue of terrorism or create controversy out of steps taken to combat it, but rather to play their role in fighting it. Bilawal also spoke Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, saying he had the right to criticise the government’s policies, and that there should certainly be room for difference of opinion in the country. He said the PPP had always imposed emergency through constitutional and legal means. “In fact, during the 2008–2013 government, when emergency rule was imposed in Balochistan, it was also because of the terrorism situation, and governor’s rule was imposed there against the PPP’s own government. “If the PPP thought only of itself, how would it have removed its own government?“ He said Fazl’s party has also been affected by terrorist attacks, so he hoped the JUI-F chief would criticise the PPP politically as much as he wished, but also condemned the terrorists. Bilawal added that if Fazl made an effort, harmony between the government and the opposition could be achieved.

items.title: ‎Burkina/ Justice : 33 dossiers inscrits à la première session du pôle ÉCOFI, dont l'affaire du trading ‎
items.description: ‎La chambre correctionnelle du pôle judiciaire spécialisé dans la répression des infractions économiques et financières et de la criminalité organisée (pôle ÉCOFI) du Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) Ouaga I tient sa première session de l'année judiciaire 2026-2027 du 19 au 30 octobre 2026. Au total, 33 dossiers sont inscrits au rôle, dont l'affaire dite « du trading », qui concerne plus d'un millier de victimes et des fonds collectés estimés à plusieurs dizaines de milliards de francs CFA. Dans un communiqué daté du 16 octobre 2026, le procureur du Faso près le TGI Ouaga I informe la population de la tenue de cette session judiciaire, prévue du lundi 19 au vendredi 30 octobre 2026. Les audiences se dérouleront à partir de 9 heures, simultanément dans les salles d'audience n° 1 et Attiron du Tribunal, conformément aux rôles établis. ‎ ‎Parmi les 33 dossiers inscrits figure l'affaire dite « du trading », référencée sous les numéros RP n° 212/2019 et RI n° 008/2019. Elle sera appelée à l'audience du lundi 19 octobre 2026. Dans cette affaire, les sociétés Globumi SA, Barka Finance International SARL et Royal Finance SARL, l'association Club des Jeunes Entreprenants du Burkina Faso (CJEBF), ainsi que neuf personnes physiques sont poursuivies, notamment pour escroquerie aggravée, blanchiment de capitaux et, pour certaines, soustraction frauduleuse au paiement de l'impôt. ‎ ‎Le procureur du Faso invite les victimes de cette affaire, ainsi que celles des autres dossiers inscrits au rôle, à se présenter aux audiences, personnellement ou par l'intermédiaire de leur conseil. Elles devront se munir d'une pièce d'identité et de tout document permettant de justifier leur préjudice, afin de se constituer partie civile et de faire valoir leurs droits. Le parquet rappelle par ailleurs que toute personne poursuivie bénéficie de la présomption d'innocence jusqu'à ce que sa culpabilité soit légalement établie par une décision définitive. Pour toute information complémentaire, les intéressés peuvent s'adresser au secrétariat du parquet du Faso près le TGI Ouaga I. ‎ ‎ ‎ Lefaso.net ‎ ‎

items.title: Ghana consulate to host DPE Canada 2027 launch
items.description: Ghana’s High Commissioner to Canada, Her Excellency Prof. Dora Francisca Edu-Buandoh and her staff at the Consulate-General in Toronto have been extra busy recently as they put everything in excellent shape for the official launch of Diaspora Property Expo (DPE) Canada 2027 – Ghana@70 Edition, slated for Friday, November 27, 2026, at 11:00 am. The launch will be held under the patronage of the High Commissioner. Speakers at the event will include Mr Ahmed Ibrahim, Minister for Works, Housing and Water Resources; Dr James Ato Orleans-Lindsay, President, Ghana Real Estate Developers Association (GREDA); and Mr Emmanuel Jeffrey, Acting CEO of Ghana Real Estate Agency Sector (REAC). The programme will be used to unveil the first 20 top Ghanaian exhibitors for the 2027 DPE. They include leading real estate developers, mortgage banks, financial service providers and allied service providers in Ghana’s real estate value chain. DPE is one of Africa’s biggest real estate exhibitions designed for Africans in the diaspora to explore property ownership and investment opportunities back home. It was originally launched at the Marriott Hotel in Accra in November 2024. It was then outdoored at the Ghana Embassy in Washington, DC, in January 2025 before hosting the main 2025 editions in Philadelphia in March 2025 and the Canada edition in Toronto in May 2025. The 2027 DPE will be held in two major editions: DPE Germany 2027 in March 2027 and DPE Canada 2027 from May 22 to May 23, 2027 in Toronto. According to H.E. Prof. Dora Francisca Edu-Buandoh, DPE Canada 2027 forms an integral part of the Ghana@70 celebration in Canada. She indicated that the High Commission is partnering organisers Diaspora Property Investment Ltd, Aim 2 Impact, Made in Ghana Consulting Ltd and other strategic partners to ensure only vetted and REAC-verified exhibitors are permitted to participate. That stance is to ensure 100% transparency, avoid fraudulent dealings and, in the process, make sure Ghana turns annual diaspora remittances into useful investments in the country. Minister for Works, Housing and Water Resources Mr. Ahmed Ibrahim, will speak at the launch Mr David Sey, DPE’s Communications Assistant, has also said that the launch would unveil an innovative product called ‘Lead, Contract and Close in 2 days, Guaranteed’. “It means we have been using the past months, since the 2025 editions in Philadelphia and Toronto, to gather real leads, real buyers with ready money waiting to buy, making DPE 2027 not your typical talk shop but a real big deal where exhibitors will sign contracts on the spot,” Mr Sey explained. According to the Exhibitions Coordinator of Made in Ghana Consulting Ltd, Jennifer Effah Sasu, the launch will also unveil the full roadmap to DPE 2027, including activities for Ghana Week in Toronto 2027 and the Ghana@70 Celebrations in Canada. The event is organised by Canada-based Aim 2 Impact and Accra-based Diaspora Property Investment Ltd and Made in Ghana Consulting Ltd in partnership with the Ghana High Commission in Ottawa and Ghana Consulate General in Toronto, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Works, Housing & Water Resources, Real Estate Agency Council (REAC) and Ghana Real Estate Developers Association (GREDA) DPE Canada 2027- Ghana@70 Edition, is co-sponsored by Dover Company Ltd, Chiraq Multimedia Ltd and Signum Developers.

items.title: Archbishop Ibezim fights back, as Awka Diocese rejects suspension by Primate
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Awka Diocesan Board of the Anglican Communion has rejected the purported suspension of the Archbishop of the Province of the Niger and Bishop of Awka Diocese, Most Revd Alexander Ibezim, by the Primate of All Nigeria, Most Revd Henry Ndukuba. The dispute has taken a new turn following the Board’s rejection of the Primate’s directive that Ibezim proceed on six months’ compulsory leave to allow an inquiry into allegations against him. Ndukuba had also appointed the Bishop of Aguata Diocese, Rt Revd Samuel Ezeofor, as supervising bishop of Awka Diocese and coordinating bishop of the Province of the Niger during the period of the purported leave. However, at an emergency meeting held at the Chapel of Divine Favour, Archbishop’s Palace, Ifite-Awka, the Board said the Primate should not take further action on the matter because cases concerning the dispute were pending in court. In a communiqué signed by the Diocese’s Lord Chancellor, B.E.I. Nwofor, SAN; Synod Secretary, Ven. K.E.N. Chukwukamma; and Mr Eugene Chukwudi Okonkwo, the Board warned that it could withdraw from the Church of Nigeria (Anglican Communion) and continue under the Church of England if the Primate and Ezeofor persisted in what it described as unlawful interference in the affairs of Awka Diocese. The Board said the Primate and Ezeofor should respect the courts where the allegations against Ibezim were pending, arguing that no one was above the law, regardless of position or status. “They are also aware that it is unlawful and contemptuous to disregard the court and take the law into their hands by actions which have the effect of pre-empting or anticipating the decisions of the court, such as the letter under reference,” the communiqué stated. Board questions Primate’s authority The Board argued that neither the Constitution and Canons of the Church of Nigeria (Anglican Communion) 2020 nor the Constitution and Regulations of Awka Diocese 2023 authorised the Primate to direct Ibezim to proceed on compulsory leave or appoint another bishop to assume his episcopal responsibilities. It specifically challenged Ndukuba’s reliance on Section 29(1) of the Church of Nigeria’s Constitution and Canons, saying the provision did not empower him to compel a fellow bishop and archbishop to take leave, hand over his duties or stop officiating in church activities. The Board also argued that the directive violated Section 36(5) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which guarantees the presumption of innocence for anyone charged with a criminal offence until proven guilty. It further alleged that the restriction on Ibezim’s participation in church activities infringed on his right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion under Section 38(1) of the Constitution. Questions inquiry process The Board also disputed the Primate’s explanation that the compulsory leave was intended to facilitate an impartial inquiry into the affairs of Awka Diocese and promote peace and reconciliation. Describing the explanation as a “ruse”, the Board alleged that Ndukuba had previously constituted two panels to investigate allegations against Ibezim but had withheld their reports. According to the communiqué, the first panel was constituted in a letter dated August 13, 2025, and chaired by Justice Babashola Ogunade, while the second was established in a letter dated June 17, 2026, under the chairmanship of Archbishop Blessing Enyindah. The Board alleged that the Primate had failed to submit the reports and recommendations to the Episcopal Synod for consideration, as required by Sections 75(3), (4) and (5), and 76(3), (4) and (5) of the Church of Nigeria’s Constitution and Canons. It said the provisions required the reports to be considered by the Episcopal Synod, with the relevant recommendations subjected to the approval of the Standing Committee and ratification by the General Synod. Board backs Ibezim, denies financial wrongdoing The Board affirmed that Ibezim remained the Bishop of Awka Diocese and Archbishop of the Province of the Niger, insisting that he should continue to discharge the duties of his offices. It also expressed confidence in his integrity, competence, ability and commitment to duty. “The Board unequivocally affirms that no money of Awka Diocese is missing, stolen, misused, or misappropriated by Archbishop Ibezim. Even the two panels set up by the Primate have not disclosed any indictment of financial misdeed by Archbishop Ibezim,” the communiqué stated. The Board commended Ibezim for what it described as significant infrastructural development in the diocese and urged him to continue his work without distraction. It also warned Ezeofor against interfering in the affairs of Awka Diocese, urging him to concentrate on his responsibilities as Bishop of Aguata Diocese. The Board said it would invoke the law and involve law enforcement agencies if what it described as interference continued. It further directed all organs of Awka Diocese to remain loyal to Ibezim and continue their lawful activities, warning them against accepting directives from Ezeofor that it considered interference in the diocese’s affairs. The Board said failure to comply with its directive could attract appropriate sanctions. The post Archbishop Ibezim fights back, as Awka Diocese rejects suspension by Primate appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Dele Cole: Nigeria has lost one of its finest intellectuals — Obasanjo
items.description: — Says late ambassador helped rebuild Nigeria’s international relations By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has mourned the death of Ambassador Patrick Dele Cole, describing him as one of Nigeria’s finest intellectuals and a trusted ally whose contributions to the country’s diplomacy, politics and public service were immense. Obasanjo, in a tribute to the late diplomat, said Cole’s death at the age of 86 was a profound personal loss and a significant loss to Nigeria, particularly given his contributions to the country’s foreign policy and international relations. The former president recalled that his relationship with Cole dated back several decades, when he was military Head of State and the late diplomat worked in the Cabinet Office. Their relationship deepened during Obasanjo’s civilian administration from 1999 to 2007, when Cole served as his Special Adviser on International Relations. Describing Cole as an indispensable member of his administration’s foreign policy team, Obasanjo said the late diplomat played a significant role in efforts to restore Nigeria’s international standing after years of diplomatic isolation. “Nigeria has lost one of its finest intellectual pillars, and I have lost a trusted ally whose counsel shaped pivotal moments in our nation’s history,” he said. Obasanjo explained that when he assumed office in 1999, his administration faced the challenge of reintegrating Nigeria into the international community, making Cole’s diplomatic expertise particularly valuable. “When I took office in 1999, Nigeria was emerging from isolation and desperately needed to be reintegrated into the global community. I knew I needed the finest diplomatic minds beside me, which led to his appointment as my Special Adviser on International Relations,” he said. The former president noted that advising a president with a strong personal interest in foreign policy required exceptional diplomatic skills, adding that Cole’s sophisticated understanding of international affairs made him a crucial member of his administration. According to Obasanjo, Cole travelled extensively with him on official engagements and worked behind the scenes to rebuild Nigeria’s diplomatic relationships and advance the country’s international interests. He also credited the late diplomat with contributing to the diplomatic and economic strategies that culminated in Nigeria’s historic Paris Club debt relief, describing his input as a combination of tact, economic insight and patriotism. “Dele brought unmatched tact, brilliant economic insight, and unyielding patriotism to the table,” Obasanjo said. Beyond his diplomatic responsibilities, the former president highlighted Cole’s contributions to journalism, particularly his tenure as managing director of the Daily Times, where he introduced an independent editorial board system intended to protect editorial policy from political interference. Obasanjo also recalled Cole’s service as Nigeria’s ambassador to Brazil and Argentina, describing his diplomatic assignments and media career as evidence of a life devoted to public service. “His masterful stints as Nigeria’s Ambassador to Brazil and Argentina further cemented his legacy as a titan of public service who proved that integrity and public duty can coexist beautifully,” he said. The former president expressed particular sadness over Cole’s death, which came years after the loss of his wife, Pastor Mina Dugoabere Cole, whom Obasanjo described as the family’s matriarch. He said the deaths of both parents had left a painful void in the Cole family, while expressing hope that they had been reunited in eternity. Obasanjo also offered words of encouragement to the deceased’s children, including Tonye and his siblings, urging them to remain united and preserve their father’s values. “To his children, Tonye and his siblings, my fatherly advice is to stand firm, united, and proud. The greatest monument you can build in honour of your father is to preserve his towering legacy of integrity, patriotism, and selfless service,” he said. Obasanjo urged the children to uphold their father’s principles and continue contributing to society, stressing that sustaining the values he represented would be the best way to honour his memory. He concluded by praying for divine comfort for the Cole family and the people of the Kalabari Kingdom as they mourned the late diplomat. “May the Almighty God grant the entire Cole family and the people of the Kalabari Kingdom the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss. May the noble soul of Ambassador Dele Cole find eternal rest,” he said. The post Dele Cole: Nigeria has lost one of its finest intellectuals — Obasanjo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Madiha Khayr : une nomination éclair au gouvernement, suivie d’une polémique sur des faits anciens
items.description: Nommée ministre déléguée chargée de la Formation professionnelle et de la Qualification vendredi 16 octobre, Madiha Khayr a été déchargée de ses fonctions dimanche 18 octobre, à la demande de la cheffe du gouvernement, Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri. Cette décision intervient dans un contexte de polémique autour d’un certificat médico-légal daté de 2004, diffusé sur les réseaux sociaux peu après sa nomination, et de la résurgence d’un article de presse évoquant une affaire de faux, d’usage de faux et d’escroquerie. Dans un communiqué publié ce dimanche , le Cabinet Royal indique que le Roi Mohammed VI a accepté la demande de Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri de mettre fin aux fonctions de Madiha Khayr au sein du gouvernement, conformément à l’article 47 de la Constitution. Le texte ne précise pas les motifs de cette décision. La polémique avait éclaté dans les heures suivant l’annonce de sa nomination, le 16 octobre, avec la circulation sur les réseaux sociaux d’un document présenté comme un certificat médico-légal, daté du 12 juin 2004. En parallèle, un article publié par un quotidien marocain en août de la même année, faisant état de poursuites pour faux, usage de faux, escroquerie et usurpation de fonction, a refait surface. Attribué à un médecin spécialiste en psychiatrie et en médecine légale, le certificat décrit l’état de santé de Madiha Khayr tel qu’il aurait été évalué à l’époque. Le médecin indique qu’elle était suivie depuis mars 2002 pour « des troubles névrotiques caractérisés par des manifestations anxieuses et dépressives, ainsi que par des troubles du comportement et de l’humeur ». Le document fait également état d’une « immaturité psychique et affective et d’une fragilité psychologique » que le praticien décrit comme « structurelle ». Selon le certificat, « cette vulnérabilité se traduisait notamment par une difficulté à faire face aux frustrations et aux situations de stress, susceptibles de provoquer des réactions impulsives et des comportements préjudiciables à ses propres intérêts ». Le médecin mentionne par ailleurs deux tentatives de suicide, qu’il qualifie de « très graves ». Celles-ci auraient nécessité une prise en charge en réanimation à l’hôpital militaire Mohammed V de Rabat, en février 2002, puis dans une clinique à Béni Mellal, en mai 2003. Dans ses conclusions, le praticien estime que la responsabilité de l’intéressée devait être considérée comme « très atténuée » , pour une durée qu’il ne précise pas. Ces appréciations figurent dans un document daté de 2004, dont l’authenticité, le contexte médical et les conditions de diffusion restent à examiner. Une affaire judiciaire rapportée en 2004 Parallèlement à la diffusion du certificat, un article publié le 19 août 2004 par un quotidien marocain a attiré l’attention sur une affaire judiciaire impliquant une femme prénommée Madiha. Selon le récit publié à l’époque, une femme de 29 ans, employée dans une coopérative agricole à Béni Mellal, avait été déférée devant le tribunal de première instance de Fquih Ben Salah. Elle était soupçonnée d’avoir utilisé les documents d’une médecin exerçant à l’hôpital Moulay-Ismaïl, à Kasba Tadla, pour ouvrir un compte bancaire et obtenir un chéquier. L’article faisait état de l’émission de 19 chèques sans provision, utilisés dans plusieurs villes marocaines, notamment Casablanca, Rabat, Khouribga, Oued Zem et El Kelaa des Sraghna. Les victimes mentionnées étaient des bijoutiers. La publication ne mentionne toutefois pas le nom de famille de la femme concernée et ne précise pas l’issue de la procédure judiciaire. La concomitance entre la délivrance du certificat et cette affaire judiciaire a néanmoins suscité de nombreuses interrogations. Un parcours politique et professionnel interrompu Avant son entrée au gouvernement, Madiha Khayr avait été élue députée de la circonscription de Béni Mellal sous les couleurs du Parti de l’Istiqlal. Le 8 octobre, elle avait été désignée à la présidence du groupe parlementaire istiqlalien à la Chambre des représentants, une responsabilité qu’elle a quittée après sa nomination ministérielle. Son parcours professionnel comprend notamment des fonctions à l’Office national des aéroports (ONDA), ainsi que le poste de secrétaire générale de l’Académie Mohammed VI internationale de l’aviation civile. Le Parti de l’Istiqlal a également réagi à la polémique autour du certificat médical. Dans une déclaration rapportée par la presse le 17 octobre, une source du parti a contesté la fiabilité des informations diffusées et appelé à la prudence, en invoquant notamment le respect de la vie privée. Elle a également rappelé le parcours de Madiha Khayr et souligné que les candidatures aux fonctions ministérielles faisaient l’objet de vérifications préalables. The post Madiha Khayr : une nomination éclair au gouvernement, suivie d’une polémique sur des faits anciens appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: APC PCC mobilizes all 10,000 support groups for Tinubu
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress APC Presidential Campaign Council PCC has gone all out to galvanize the party’s over 10,000 support groups as part of its grassroots mobilization strategies for the reelection of President Bola Tinubu. Consequently, the APC PCC said it has opened an online registration portal for registration and revalidation of support groups membership. Director of the Support Groups Mobilization Directorate of the 2027 APC-PCC and a former Deputy Governor of Nasarawa State, Hon. Silas Agara, announced the launch at the national secretariat of the Tinubu Support Group TSG on Sunday in Abuja. “Today, we are officially launching our online support group registration portal. The portal goes live today, 17 October 2026, and will remain open for five days, closing on 22 October 2026”, he said. He asked all groups and volunteer networks working for the President’s re-election to register within that window, “irrespective of whether they have previously registered with the party or another campaign structure.” According to him, the exercise “will enable us to verify participating groups, understand their geographical spread and organisational capacity, and establish a reliable database for effective coordination and nationwide engagement.” “I urge every group to take this exercise seriously. Our objective is to build a unified mobilisation structure that is organised, accountable, responsive and prepared for the demands of the campaign ahead,” Agara said. He described support groups as “a vital link between the party, the campaign organisation and the Nigerian people.” They “bring together communities, professional associations, interest groups and volunteers, helping to communicate the administration’s policies, explain its achievements and engage citizens on issues that matter to them,” he said. The directorate’s mandate, he added, is “to coordinate these groups, strengthen their organisational capacity and ensure that their activities complement the broader objectives of the APC presidential campaign.” Agara said the mobilisation drive is “anchored on the record of the Tinubu administration and its Renewed Hope Agenda.” “Over the past three years, President Tinubu has undertaken major economic and institutional reforms aimed at addressing longstanding structural challenges and placing Nigeria on a path towards sustainable growth,” he said. He listed “the removal of the fuel subsidy, the unification of foreign exchange rates, measures to strengthen local government autonomy and comprehensive tax reforms” among the reforms. Agara also cited the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, “which expands access to financing for eligible students,” and the Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation, “designed to broaden access to consumer credit.” On health, Agara said “the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative is supporting efforts to improve service delivery, strengthen primary healthcare and expand access to specialised treatment, including cancer care. “Our responsibility is to communicate the administration’s achievements accurately, explain its policies clearly and listen to the legitimate concerns of Nigerians,” he said. He told the groups that “the task ahead is not merely to promote a political message. It is to engage citizens respectfully, provide credible information and demonstrate that the Renewed Hope Agenda can deliver meaningful improvements in their lives. “Let us take the message to our communities, workplaces, markets and neighbourhoods. Let us build bridges across differences, promote constructive dialogue and mobilise support through credible engagement, service and responsible conduct,” he said. Agara warned that “the 2027 election will demand organisation, discipline and sustained engagement. Together, let us build a stronger mobilisation platform in support of national development, shared prosperity and the Renewed Hope Agenda,” he said. The post APC PCC mobilizes all 10,000 support groups for Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kebbi Govt slams Malami over UNDP poverty report claim
items.description: The Kebbi Government has taken a swipe at the African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate, Abubakar Malami, SAN. The government faulted the ADC guber candidate’s use of a UNDP poverty report to criticise the APC-led administration in the state. The Commissioner for Information and Culture, Alhaji Yakubu Ahmed-BK, slammed Malami at a press briefing in Birnin Kebbi on Sunday. He alleged that the former Attorney-General of the Federation was exploiting the report to score political points ahead of the 2027 general elections, rather than offering constructive solutions to the state’s challenges. Ahmed-BK said one property reportedly ordered for confiscation in Birnin Kebbi in court proceedings involving the former minister could have funded more than 1,000 boreholes across the state. He said the government acknowledged the economic difficulties and security challenges confronting Nigeria, but accused Malami of politicising the hardship of the people for personal political advantage. Ahmed-BK expressed surprise that Malami, who served as Attorney-General of the Federation under the late President Muhammadu Buhari, was now using the poverty report to criticise the state government. According to him, the period covered by the UNDP report included the first term and part of the second term of the Buhari administration, during which Malami held a prominent position. He alleged that policies and actions during the previous administration contributed to the economic difficulties reflected in the report. Ahmed-BK also accused Malami of failing to adequately address insecurity in Kebbi during his time in the Federal Government, despite his influential position. He referred to reports published in June 2025 concerning alleged killings in Tadurga Ward of Zuru Emirate. “Malami’s reported figure of 200 deaths was subsequently disputed by local security agencies, government officials and the Zuru Emirate Council. “The subsequent clarifications reportedly put the death toll at fewer than 30. Malami just used the incident for political purposes,” he said. He accused the former minister of hypocrisy over the relationship between poverty and alleged corruption, citing court proceedings involving the confiscation of properties allegedly linked to him. Ahmed-BK argued that the allegations and court proceedings involving the former minister should be considered when assessing his criticism of the state’s poverty levels. He also accused some former public office holders of seeking elective positions to shield themselves from accountability. On security, Ahmed-BK said the administration of Gov. Nasir Idris had taken several steps to strengthen security and support personnel combating banditry and other violent crimes across the state. He said the government had procured and donated hundreds of operational vehicles and thousands of motorcycles to security agencies. “These include the provision of welfare support to soldiers, police officers, personnel of the Department of State Services (DSS), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), hunters and vigilante groups. “The Governor has also visited communities affected by attacks to sympathise with victims, provide relief and assure residents of additional measures to improve security. “The administration has facilitated the establishment of forward operating bases and other military formations. “The formations include the 28 Armoured Brigade and Garrison in Birnin Kebbi, the 281 Tank Battalion in Yauri and the 381 Artillery Regiment in Kaoje,” he said. Ahmed-BK added that the state government was procuring additional armoured platforms to enhance security operations. On the government’s development agenda, the commissioner listed investments in health, education, road construction, economic empowerment, agricultural support, employment and workers’ welfare among the administration’s priorities. He said the government had distributed free fertilisers and other farming inputs, provided solar-powered and compressed natural gas (CNG)-powered pumps for wet- and dry-season farming, distributed food items and employed thousands of teachers. According to him, the administration had improved wages, paid scholarships and provided support for the registration and school fees of students studying within and outside Nigeria, as well as implemented cash-transfer interventions worth billions of Naira. Ahmed-BK described the administration’s road construction programme as a deliberate effort to addressing longstanding infrastructure deficits, particularly those affecting farmers and commercial activities. He cited the Koko-Zuru Road as an important agricultural and economic corridor, saying its poor condition over the years had affected the movement of farm produce and other goods. On solid minerals development, the commissioner said the state government had established a Ministry of Solid Minerals Development and a Solid Minerals Development Agency to regulate the sector, protect the interests of residents and attract investment. He said the government was in advanced discussions with local and foreign investors, adding that agreements had been signed and credit facilities advanced towards prospective investments. The commissioner acknowledged that the administration’s efforts had yet to fully address the poverty challenges facing the state. He argued that the scale of the problems required sustained interventions beyond the government’s first three years in office. Ahmed-BK called on the people of Kebbi to support the Idris administration, popularly known as Kauran Gwandu. “I urge the residents to give the administration another term, as continuity will enable ongoing projects and policies to deliver greater benefits to the state,” the commissioner pleaded. The post Kebbi Govt slams Malami over UNDP poverty report claim appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Otti raises scholarship award to ₦350,000, rewards six first-class graduates
items.description: …Foundation inducts 81 new scholars By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has increased the annual scholarship award of the Alex Otti Foundation (AOF) from ₦250,000 to ₦350,000 per beneficiary and rewarded six first-class graduates with ₦500,000 each. Otti announced the increase on Saturday at the Foundation’s 2026 Scholarship Banquet, held at the Michael Okpara Auditorium, Umuahia, where 81 new scholars were inducted into the programme. The governor, who attributed the increase to prevailing economic realities, directed the Foundation to extend the new award to existing beneficiaries who were still in school. He said the scholarship programme was strictly merit-based, stressing that political affiliation, family background and social connections played no role in selecting beneficiaries. “Once you qualify, you are taken. It doesn’t matter your political affiliation. We don’t want to know who your parents support or where you come from,” Otti said. He challenged the beneficiaries to justify the investment in their education by striving for academic excellence and producing more first-class graduates in subsequent years. The six beneficiaries who graduated with first-class honours this year received ₦500,000 each in recognition of their academic achievements. Otti urged the scholars to remain humble, grateful and committed to their studies, warning them against arrogance and a sense of entitlement. He recounted his visit to injured police officers attacked by hoodlums and other patients receiving treatment at a hospital in Aba, saying the experience reminded him of the difficult circumstances many people faced through no fault of their own. “When you think that you have arrived, when you become self-conceited, when you become arrogant, don’t go too far, just visit a hospital, you will come out humbled,” he said. The governor urged the students to appreciate the opportunity provided by the Foundation and use their education to make meaningful contributions to society. He also stressed that the Foundation’s activities were independent of politics and would continue beyond his political career. Foundation tracks 302 scholars Earlier, the Executive Secretary of the Foundation, Chidiebere Nnanna, said the induction of the 81 new beneficiaries brought to 302 the number of scholars whose progress had been tracked since 2019. He disclosed that more than 81 beneficiaries had already graduated, describing the initiative as an investment in the future of young people rather than mere financial assistance. According to him, the Foundation aims to help beneficiaries complete their education, build careers and pursue higher degrees, while expanding opportunities for leadership development and career preparation. Nnanna attributed the programme’s progress to the commitment of its founder, Otti, whom he described as a firm believer in education as a tool for overcoming poverty and ignorance. He congratulated the new scholars and expressed confidence that they would excel academically and become sources of inspiration and opportunities for others. Speaking on behalf of the six first-class graduates, Chizaram Okoronkwo, a graduate of the Faculty of Nursing Science at Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Anambra State, thanked Otti and the Foundation for their financial support. She said the scholarship had eased her financial burden and enabled her to concentrate on her studies. Okoronkwo recalled that the governor increased the scholarship award from ₦150,000 to ₦250,000 in 2023, describing the latest increase as another demonstration of confidence in students and investment in their future. The event was attended by the Deputy Governor, Ikechukwu Emetu; government officials; captains of industry; and parents and families of the beneficiaries. The post Otti raises scholarship award to ₦350,000, rewards six first-class graduates appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nnamdi Kanu: Family accuses Britain of failing detained citizen
items.description: …Faults conviction under repealed law, alleges judicial irregularities …Says appeal filed in June remains unheard By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The family of detained Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) leader, Nnamdi Kanu, has accused the British Government of failing to secure justice for him, demanding urgent diplomatic action over his continued detention and an appeal it says remains unheard. The family, in a statement issued on Sunday by Prince Emmanuel Kanu on behalf of the Okwu-Kanu Family, said Britain’s diplomatic engagements had failed to secure Kanu’s release, a hearing of his appeal or a meaningful resolution of the legal issues surrounding his conviction. Kanu, a British citizen, is serving a life sentence in Nigeria following his conviction in November 2025. His family maintains that the conviction was based on repealed legislation and violates Section 36(12) of the Nigerian Constitution, which prohibits conviction for a criminal offence unless the offence and its penalty are prescribed in a written law. The family challenged the Nigerian authorities to identify the specific provisions of extant law under which Kanu was convicted, arguing that a savings clause could not substitute for an applicable written-law provision defining the offences and prescribing their penalties. It described the legal questions surrounding the conviction as fundamental constitutional issues that should not be dismissed as mere technicalities. The family also questioned Kanu’s continued detention after the Court of Appeal discharged him and quashed the charges against him in October 2022. It alleged that he remained in detention for about 14 months after the appellate court’s decision and accused the Federal Government of subsequently prosecuting him on counts it said had already been quashed. The family further questioned the use of a civil process to stay the execution of the appellate court’s decision, describing the sequence of events as a serious challenge to the rule of law. It also expressed concern that Kanu’s appeal, which it said was filed and served in June 2026, had yet to be listed for hearing as of October 18. Demands answers from Britain The family urged the British Government to move beyond routine consular visits and disclose the concrete steps it had taken to address the case. It specifically asked whether Kanu’s case had been referred to the United Kingdom’s Envoy for Complex Consular Detentions, appointed in July 2026, and urged the Foreign Secretary to refer it urgently if this had not been done. Describing the consular contact it had experienced as inadequate, the family said occasional telephone calls to inquire about Kanu’s welfare could not substitute for effective action on the legal and human rights concerns it had raised. It demanded that Britain press for an early hearing of Kanu’s appeal and seek a lawful resolution of the issues surrounding his detention. “We demand action, not engagement. We demand answers, not consular visits,” the statement declared. Invokes Britain’s civil war record The family also linked Britain’s current handling of Kanu’s case to its historical role in the Nigerian Civil War, accusing the British Government of prioritising strategic interests over Biafra. Citing a United States intelligence assessment dated August 12, 1969, and parliamentary proceedings of November 17, 1969, it alleged that Britain continued supplying arms to the Nigerian Federal Government during the war despite publicly advocating peace. It argued that Britain’s response to Kanu’s detention would test its professed commitment to the rule of law and the protection of British citizens abroad. The family stressed that it was not asking Britain to determine the outcome of Kanu’s appeal but to use its diplomatic influence to ensure that his legal challenges received appropriate attention. According to the statement, Kanu remains detained at the Sokoto Correctional Centre, with the family expressing concern about his health and prolonged loss of liberty. The family called on the British and Nigerian governments to provide clear answers on the legal basis of his conviction, the status of his appeal and the steps being taken to address the issues raised. The allegations and legal interpretations in the statement represent the family’s position. The post Nnamdi Kanu: Family accuses Britain of failing detained citizen appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: Opposition woke up too late to stop Tinubu — Adebayo
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Chief Communications Adviser to the Adebayo-Bugaje Presidential Campaign, Comrade Mark Adebayo, has said opposition parties seeking a common presidential ticket may have waited too long to build the political structures needed to defeat President Bola Tinubu in 2027. Speaking with Vanguard in Abuja, Adebayo said the challenge goes beyond agreeing on a single candidate, arguing that the opposition should have started building the political infrastructure for a coalition at least three years ago. He, however, insisted that defeating Tinubu remains possible with the right strategy and mass mobilisation. “The conversations around different political parties coming together to support a single presidential ticket came too late in the day, in my opinion. That’s a conversation that should have begun at least three years ago by building critical political infrastructures to achieve that. “You can’t start such a crucial process on the eve of a general election,” Adebayo added. He also identified differences in the political and governance ideologies of the parties and their candidates as another major obstacle to a united opposition. “I think the opposition woke up to that realization too late,” Adebayo said. “Meanwhile, whilst I agree it is extremely challenging, it is not impossible for one presidential candidate to defeat the incumbent.” Adebayo expressed confidence that Prince Adewole Adebayo could defeat Tinubu through a broad-based movement against the current system of governance. “With the application of the appropriate strategies predicated on massive mobilization of Nigerians around a movement to end this ‘corrupt’ and ‘satanic’ system that is killing our country, it is possible for an opposition candidate to defeat Tinubu next year and Prince Adewole Adebayo is working so hard to achieve that,” he said. items.title: Zamfara deputy governor reportedly trapped by angry youths
items.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau GUSAU — Zamfara State Deputy Governor, Mani Malam Mumini, was reportedly trapped by angry youths in Gwashi town, Bukkuyum Local Government Area, on Sunday, during a visit to commiserate with residents over a recent bandit attack. Sources said the youths barricaded the entrance to the town, chanting “Bamayi”, which means “We don’t want you”, accusing the government of failing to protect them from banditry. The deputy governor was reportedly visiting the community to offer condolences following an attack by bandits that claimed the lives of at least nine security operatives and several civilians. Residents who spoke to Vanguard by telephone said the community was angered by what they described as the government’s failure to visit the area or commiserate with victims in the immediate aftermath of the attack. They accused the state government of abandoning them during their moment of grief and only visiting days after the incident. “The people are angry. We lost nine security personnel and many innocent citizens. Nobody from government came when we were under attack and mourning our people. Now they are here, we don’t want them,” the residents said. The situation reportedly escalated, forcing the deputy governor and his security detail to seek cover amid fears that the angry youths could attack them. Residents said the incident reflected growing frustration over insecurity in Bukkuyum Local Government Area, which has been among the areas affected by banditry in Zamfara State. They expressed dissatisfaction with what they described as inadequate government efforts to protect lives and property in the community. As of the time of filing this report, the deputy governor and his entourage were reportedly stranded in the area, awaiting reinforcements to facilitate their safe departure from the community. There was no immediate official statement from the state government on the incident. The post Zamfara deputy governor reportedly trapped by angry youths appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: I won’t step down for ADC, Kwankwaso declares
items.description: …says party no better than APC By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, vice-presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has ruled out withdrawing from the 2027 presidential race in favour of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, declaring that the opposition party offers no better alternative to the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC. Kwankwaso’s declaration comes amid opposition manoeuvres ahead of the election, with the NDC chieftain accusing the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, PCC, of promoting claims that his ticket with Peter Obi is working for the APC or may step down for the ADC candidate at the last minute. In a statement on Sunday, Kwankwaso accused the ADC campaign team of directing unnecessary attacks at him, Obi and the NDC instead of selling its own candidate to Nigerians. “We will not withdraw our candidature for the ADC or any other party,” he declared. Kwankwaso also dismissed suggestions that the NDC ticket was acting on behalf of the ruling party, insisting that it remained committed to contesting the election. “The OK ticket is neither working for nor acting on behalf of the APC or any of its candidates. We see no possibility or reason to withdraw from the presidential race in favour of the ADC candidate or any other,” he said. Turning his attention to the ADC campaign council, Kwankwaso urged it to address allegations levelled against its presidential candidate by Vice-President Kashim Shettima rather than attack the NDC ticket. He also rejected the ADC’s claim to being an alternative to the APC-led government, which he accused of failing Nigerians. “The APC-led government has failed Nigerians. The ADC offers no better alternative,” Kwankwaso declared. Presenting the NDC as a stronger opposition platform, he said his ticket with Obi had the credibility, capacity and nationwide support to unite the country and tackle insecurity, education, agriculture, infrastructure, healthcare and economic challenges. Kwankwaso urged supporters and well-meaning Nigerians to remain committed to the party’s electoral victory, describing the NDC as the country’s most formidable opposition party. “I therefore urge all our supporters and well-meaning Nigerians to continue working toward the victory of our great party,” he said. items.title: NSITF inaugurates anti-corruption unit to boost accountability
items.description: …ICPC chairman describes move as step towards strengthening integrity and public trust By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — The Managing Director and Chief Executive of the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF), Oluwaseun Faleye, has described the inauguration of the Fund’s Anti-Corruption and Transparency Unit (ACTU) as a renewed commitment to promoting integrity, accountability and public trust. Faleye spoke in Abuja during the inauguration of the NSITF ACTU and its regional and branch champions at the Fund’s headquarters. Welcoming a delegation from the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), led by a representative of its chairman, Faleye described the commission as a partner in promoting compliance and supporting institutional reforms. He said the inauguration followed efforts to establish the unit and expressed satisfaction that the process had been completed. “It has truly been a long day coming. We have been at this for a bit, and I am glad we have finally found a way to do this,” he said. Faleye said the presence of the ICPC delegation reflected the collaborative relationship between the two agencies, adding that the NSITF viewed engagement with the anti-corruption commission as an opportunity to learn and improve. “Our shared commitment to protecting and promoting transparency, accountability and ethical conduct in public service is one reason we feel collaboration is very important,” he said. He described the inauguration as more than a formal exercise, saying it represented a renewed commitment to building an institution guided by integrity and accountability. “For us at NSITF, today’s inauguration is much more than a formal exercise. It is really a renewed commitment to the kind of institution we want NSITF to be. One where integrity guides our conduct, accountability defines our actions, and public trust remains central,” he said. The NSITF chief executive allayed fears that the unit was established to witch-hunt staff, explaining that its mandate was preventive and collaborative rather than investigative or interrogative. “There is really no cause for concern. It is not a witch-hunt, it is not an investigative or interrogative process. It is rather a collaborative process that guides us from making mistakes we will regret down the line,” he said. He urged staff to regard the unit as a partner and encouraged its members to engage colleagues in ways that would make them comfortable sharing information and reporting suspected wrongdoing where necessary. Faleye charged the newly inaugurated members and regional and branch champions to discharge their duties with integrity, objectivity, courage and professionalism. He said the unit’s credibility would depend not merely on its existence but on its impact on the Fund’s integrity and accountability. The managing director said the appointment of regional and branch champions was crucial to extending the anti-corruption initiative beyond the headquarters, noting that much of the Fund’s operations took place at the regional and branch levels. He stressed that preventing corruption was the responsibility of every staff member, regardless of rank, and not the ACTU alone. “Every staff member has a duty to uphold established procedures, protect public resources and act in the best interest of the institution,” he said. Faleye assured that the management would continue to strengthen internal controls, encourage ethical behaviour and lead by example. “Internal control, ethical behaviour, accountability will start from the top and go down the ranks. We are committed to providing the right leadership,” he added. ACTU members pledge commitment to integrity Speaking on behalf of the newly inaugurated ACTU members, the Deputy General Manager, General Administration Services, at the NSITF Abuja Regional Office, Asma’u Mohammed, pledged to discharge the unit’s mandate with diligence, objectivity and professionalism. She expressed appreciation to the Fund’s management, particularly Faleye, for the confidence reposed in the members and what she described as his commitment to institutional integrity. “We wish to express our sincere appreciation to the Management of NSITF, under the visionary leadership of our Managing Director/Chief Executive, Mr Oluwaseun Faleye, for the confidence reposed in us. We are deeply honoured by this responsibility and fully conscious of the expectations that accompany it,” she said. Mohammed also thanked the ICPC chairman and management for their continued support and guidance in strengthening integrity systems across public institutions. She said the inauguration represented a renewed commitment to embedding transparency and accountability in the Fund’s operations. According to her, the ACTU would promote ethical values, identify and mitigate corruption risks, encourage compliance with established procedures and support management in strengthening good governance. Mohammed welcomed the inauguration of regional and branch champions alongside the national members, saying the initiative would extend integrity advocacy to every level of the Fund. “This initiative represents an important step towards extending integrity advocacy to every level of the Fund. Through this network, we hope to strengthen awareness, encourage ethical conduct, and ensure that the values we uphold are reflected in our daily activities across all NSITF offices,” she said. She pledged that members would work with management, staff and relevant stakeholders to strengthen ethical standards, promote transparency and reinforce institutional safeguards. Mohammed said the members accepted the responsibility with determination to justify the confidence placed in them and contribute to greater public trust and service delivery. ICPC chairman backs initiative Inaugurating the unit, ICPC Chairman, Dr Musa Adamu Aliyu, SAN, described its establishment as an important step towards strengthening integrity and accountability within the NSITF. Aliyu thanked the Fund’s management and staff for their support in facilitating the inauguration and induction of the unit’s members. He said the exercise would strengthen the Fund’s internal mechanisms for promoting integrity, transparency and accountability while equipping members with the knowledge needed to perform their duties effectively. The ICPC chairman recalled that ACTUs were established through a collaboration between the commission and the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation (OHCSF) and had evolved into a recognised anti-corruption platform within the public service. “They serve as internal mechanisms for identifying systemic weaknesses, mitigating corruption risks, promoting ethical conduct and strengthening compliance with established rules and procedures,” he said. Aliyu said the initiative aligned with the NSITF’s vision of becoming Africa’s leading social security institution and advancing social policy, economic empowerment and poverty alleviation. He stressed that the ACTU was not a rival to management but a complementary unit operating under the oversight of the managing director. “It is important to emphasise that the ACTU is a complementary unit to Management. Its role is not to compete with or replace the Management but to support and strengthen the Fund’s efforts in promoting transparency, accountability, and ethical practices,” he said. Aliyu urged the NSITF management to provide the unit with an enabling environment, adequate funding, appropriate office facilities and representation on relevant standing committees. He also encouraged the Fund to invite the ICPC to observe promotion, recruitment and procurement exercises to enhance transparency and public confidence in the processes. Congratulating the newly inaugurated members, the ICPC chairman described their appointment as both a privilege and a call to service. He urged them to discharge their duties with diligence, integrity, impartiality and professionalism, warning them against relationships or actions that could undermine their independence and credibility. Aliyu reaffirmed the commission’s commitment to working with the NSITF to promote good governance and national development. He said the inauguration reinforced the shared commitment of both institutions to transparency, accountability and ethical standards in the public service. ACTU chairperson calls for collective action In her remarks, the Acting Chairperson of the NSITF ACTU, Udoka Mirian Otti, said the fight against corruption required the commitment and participation of every staff member. She described the programme as an important step towards strengthening anti-corruption awareness and promoting ethical conduct within the Fund. “It is my pleasure to welcome you all to this important programme marking the inauguration and onboarding of our ACTU Champions and the promotion of anti-corruption awareness within the Fund,” she said. Otti said the unit had a vital role in promoting integrity, transparency, accountability and ethical behaviour across the organisation. She noted that, as an institution responsible for providing social security protection to Nigerian workers and their dependants under the Employees’ Compensation Scheme, the NSITF must ensure that its actions and internal processes reflected fairness, responsibility and accountability. Otti thanked the ICPC for its continued guidance and collaboration, as well as the NSITF management for supporting efforts to strengthen transparency and accountability within the Fund.
