items.title: Man arrested for unlawful possession of firearms, suspected Indian hemp in Kpando
items.description: A 31-year-old man, Saviour Dzadze, has been arrested in Kpando by the Volta North Regional Police Command for unlawful possession of firearms and suspected Indian hemp on Wednesday, 14th October, 2026. The arrest follows a death threat complaint by one Dzodzi Kofi Kpakpamikpe on October 8th, 2026, compelling the police to search the house of Saviour, the suspect. This was contained in a communique signed by the Volta North Regional Public Relations Officer, Inspr. Felix Kwao, and copied to Myjoyonline.com. Saviour Dzadze was arrested at the premises of the Kpando Circuit Court after the police found guns and ammunition at his residence. The items found included an AK-47 Assault rifle, a pump-action shotgun, a locally manufactured single-barrel gun, 10 AAA lion cartridges and some quantity of substances suspected to be Indian Hemp. “Investigation further established that the suspect traded his cultivated suspected Indian hemp for the AK-47 Assault rifle to an unidentified man from Togo. He received the pump-action shotgun from his brother Foster Dzadze in Accra while he inherited the locally manufactured single-barrel gun from his late father Mathereous Dzadze”, stated Inspr. Felix Kwao The suspect is currently in police custody assisting the investigation and is expected to appear before the law court on Friday October 16th, 2026 to answer for his charges. “The Volta North Regional Police Command reiterated its commitment to fighting crime while efforts are underway to arrest his accomplices to assist the police investigation”, Inspr. Felix Kwao concluded.

items.title: Two dead after galamsey pit collapses at Sefwi Datano
items.description: Two people have died after a galamsey pit collapsed on them at Sefwi Datano in the Bodi District of the Western North Region. The deceased, identified as Kwaku Charles and Nana Dibi, are believed to be in their early thirties. They were reportedly digging for gold at a site where they regularly worked when the pit collapsed. According to reports, the two were working with a third person who is currently unaccounted for when the incident occurred. Residents and community members rushed to the site to assist in the rescue effort. An excavator was brought in to help retrieve the trapped miners, but the operation reportedly resulted in the head of one of the victims being severed before the bodies were recovered. Confirming the incident to Adom News, Datano Unit Committee member Joseph Debrah said he received a distress call that two people had been trapped in a galamsey pit. He said he alerted community leaders, who mobilised some of the youth to the site to support the rescue operation. The police in Bodi were also informed and joined the effort to retrieve the bodies. The remains were subsequently transported to the Juaboso Government Hospital mortuary for preservation, while further investigations are expected to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident. The tragedy has cast a pall of grief over the Sefwi Datano community and renewed concerns about the dangers associated with illegal small-scale mining.

items.title: Plateau records 11,000 TB cases in 2026
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — Plateau State has recorded an estimated 11,000 tuberculosis (TB) cases in 2026, with 2,047 patients identified and placed on treatment between July and September. The Monitoring and Evaluation Officer of the Plateau State Tuberculosis and Leprosy Control Programme, Yohanna Bot, disclosed this in Jos during the first bi-annual media-focused advocacy meeting on the Global Fund AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria Integrated Community-Led Monitoring (ICLM) Project. Bot described tuberculosis as a significant public health challenge in the state, attributing its spread to its airborne nature, overcrowding, malnutrition, weakened immune systems and other risk factors. “Based on the prevalence rate of 219 per 100,000 population, we have over 11,000 people with TB in the state. “We just completed our quarterly survey, and from the analysis, we discovered that between July and September, 2,047 patients were identified and placed on treatment,” he said. He added that the patients were receiving treatment at various health centres across the state. According to Bot, children under five, older people and people living with HIV are particularly vulnerable to the disease because of weakened immune systems. He also identified stigma and misconceptions about tuberculosis as major barriers to early diagnosis and treatment, noting that some residents still attributed the disease to spiritual or ritual causes. Bot said insecurity and displacement had further complicated efforts to detect cases, particularly in Mangu, Jos South and Barkin Ladi, where violence had led to the establishment of camps for internally displaced persons (IDPs). “Overcrowding in these camps facilitates the rapid transmission of the disease,” he said. On measures to contain the spread, Bot said the programme was prioritising community outreach, particularly in IDP camps and correctional centres, to identify cases through active screening. He said patients who tested positive were placed on treatment, adding that effective treatment could render them non-infectious within about two weeks. Bot, however, raised concerns over shortages of anti-TB drugs, attributing the gaps in availability to supply chain disruptions and the programme’s heavy reliance on international support, particularly the Global Fund. He called for increased public awareness to address misconceptions and stigma surrounding tuberculosis, urging residents to seek medical attention rather than rely on unfounded beliefs. Speaking at the meeting, the Plateau State Programme Officer of the Global Fund AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria Integrated Community-Led Monitoring Project, Peter Ezekiel, said Nigeria ranked first in Africa and sixth globally among countries with a high burden of tuberculosis and TB/HIV co-infection. He added that Nigeria also had the world’s highest number of people affected by malaria and the second-largest HIV/AIDS burden globally. Ezekiel said the co-occurrence of malaria and tuberculosis among people living with HIV posed additional health challenges, as co-infections could worsen illness and complicate treatment. Explaining the project’s approach, he said ATM Networks were using community-led monitoring to mobilise stakeholders to participate in, own and support health interventions, particularly those addressing HIV/AIDS, malaria and tuberculosis. According to him, the approach helps identify gaps affecting healthcare delivery and access, including gender-related barriers, discrimination and stigma, while enabling communities to advocate increased domestic funding and improved healthcare infrastructure. Highlighting the project’s achievements in Plateau, Ezekiel said the initiative had mobilised resources for infrastructure rehabilitation, service improvements, health systems strengthening and greater community participation since implementation began in the state. “From June till date, we have repaired and re-piped toilet facilities at the Primary Health Centre (PHC), Rantya, Jos South. Community stakeholders also donated a brand-new scanning machine and 10 iron-framed chairs to PHC Gangare in Jos North, BP apparatus to PHC Dogon Agogo and new hospital bed mattresses to PHC Pushit,” he said. He said other interventions included the purchase and donation of TB sputum cups to the COCIN Rehabilitation Centre in Mangu Local Government Area and the provision of 500 copies of clients’ enrolment forms through community efforts. Ezekiel added that residents of Lamingo had jointly mobilised resources and engaged security personnel to protect night-shift staff and property at PHC Lamingo, with an agreement to pay ₦15,000 monthly. He said the interventions had strengthened infection prevention measures, improved patients’ experiences and enhanced healthcare delivery. Ezekiel called for greater collaboration among government agencies, healthcare providers and community stakeholders, stressing the need for preventive measures, treatment, health education and community partnerships. He also advocated expanding national and state health insurance programmes to cover vulnerable citizens, particularly low-income earners, alongside adequate funding for primary healthcare and greater accountability in the management of health resources. Also speaking, the Director of Disease Control and Immunisation at the Plateau State Primary Health Care Board, Dr Yakubu Izang, said community-led monitoring was essential to improving healthcare delivery at the grassroots. He said the approach helped identify gaps and challenges that government agencies might otherwise overlook, enabling stakeholders to work together to develop solutions. items.title: NLC, Falana, activists rally Nigerians against fuel price hike
items.description: .. .Accuse FG of enriching few at expense of citizens .. .Say workers, masses under siege …Describe ₦70,000 minimum wage as cruel joke By Victor Ahiuma-Young & Henry Obetta Labour leaders and pro-democracy activists have called on Nigerians to unite against rising petrol prices and worsening economic hardship, accusing the Federal Government of implementing policies that impoverish workers and the masses while enriching a privileged few. They warned that rising pump prices of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), popularly known as petrol, had eroded workers’ purchasing power, deepened poverty and pushed millions of Nigerians into a daily struggle for survival. The activists, including the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), human rights lawyer, Femi Falana, SAN, and members of the Joint Action Front (JAF), made the call at the weekend in Lagos during a symposium held as part of the first memorial celebration in honour of Comrade Abiodun Aremu. NLC President, Joe Ajaero, represented by the union’s Acting General Secretary, Benson Upah, said the removal of the petrol subsidy had inflicted devastating consequences on workers and the wider population, insisting that organised labour would continue to demand relief from the Federal Government. In an address delivered on his behalf, Ajaero described the prevailing economic situation as a crisis of survival, arguing that workers could no longer cope with rising transport fares, food prices, electricity tariffs and the depreciation of the naira. “The removal of the fuel subsidy has devastated Nigeria’s working class and masses,” the address stated. According to the NLC, rising transport costs have forced many workers to choose between paying exorbitant fares and walking long distances to their workplaces. The union also cited increases in the prices of essential commodities, noting that a bag of rice that previously sold for about ₦30,000 now costs more than ₦80,000, while the price of a loaf of bread has risen from approximately ₦500 to ₦1,500. It further argued that rising electricity tariffs had forced some small businesses to shut down, while the depreciation of the naira had increased the cost of imported medicines, industrial inputs and other essential goods. The labour movement attributed the worsening conditions to what it described as anti-people economic policies implemented without adequate consultation or effective measures to cushion their impact. “The government has effectively declared war on its own people, pushing the majority to the fringes of survival,” the address declared. The NLC said the crisis reflected economic policies that, in its view, enriched the ruling class while deepening the hardship experienced by ordinary citizens. NLC issues ultimatum over petrol prices The NLC disclosed that it issued a two-week ultimatum to the Federal Government on October 9, demanding an immediate reduction in petrol prices. According to the address, the ultimatum was intended to compel the government to address the growing disconnect between workers’ earnings and the cost of living. Ajaero said: “Most recently, the NLC issued a two-week ultimatum to the Federal Government, demanding an immediate reduction in the price of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), also known as petrol. “This ultimatum is not a mere bargaining chip but a solemn warning. If the government does not act within the stipulated timeframe, the NLC will have no choice but to seek remedial steps with all of us in this hall today.” He argued that petrol prices should be reduced to a level consistent with the purchasing power of workers earning the national minimum wage of ₦70,000 monthly. The NLC recalled that when the minimum wage was set at ₦70,000 in July 2024, petrol sold for approximately ₦668.30 per litre, compared with prices exceeding ₦1,400 per litre in many parts of the country at the time of the symposium. “A worker earning ₦70,000 a month cannot afford to buy petrol at ₦1,400 per litre. The government has effectively rendered the minimum wage meaningless. “The ₦70,000 minimum wage was inadequate when it was announced. It is now a cruel joke. The NLC will not accept a situation where Nigerian workers are expected to survive on starvation wages while the cost of living continues to rise,” Ajaero declared. Beyond demanding a reduction in petrol prices, the NLC urged the government to take concrete measures to stabilise the naira, reduce inflation and strengthen domestic refining capacity. “The removal of the subsidy was justified on the grounds that it would attract investment in local refining. Where is that investment? “The struggle against the fuel subsidy removal is a struggle for democracy, because a policy that is imposed on the people without their consent, and against their will, is the antithesis of democracy. “And it is a struggle for survival, because the removal of the subsidy has made it impossible for millions of Nigerians to meet their basic needs,” the address stated. Falana questions government’s approach to fuel pricing Falana, chairman of the event, challenged the argument that withdrawing the petrol subsidy was the only viable option available to the government, pointing to the continued use of subsidies in other countries. “As you are all aware, countries across the world, including major capitalist economies such as the United States, Germany and France, subsidise not only fuel but also education, healthcare and other essential services. “That is the reality today. A simple internet search will reveal announcements of various subsidies in different countries,” he said. The senior advocate argued that governments should consider different policy options to protect citizens from economic shocks rather than treat subsidy removal as unavoidable. He also referred to international developments concerning energy supplies and sanctions against Russia, arguing that countries routinely reconsider their economic positions in response to changing circumstances. Falana criticised the Federal Government’s position on petrol prices, saying Nigerians continued to face high costs despite official discussions about reducing the commodity’s landed cost. “Here in Nigeria, with elections approaching, the government is telling us that the best it can offer is that the landed cost of fuel will be ₦1,350 per litre. “When the government talks about landed cost, we must consider what that means for Nigerians in Abuja, Jos, Maiduguri and other parts of the country, where additional transportation and distribution costs may apply. That is what this administration has offered the Nigerian people. “Among those seeking to take over power, only a few, including Omoyele Sowore and Donald Duke, have reportedly stated that, if given the opportunity, they would ensure that fuel sells for less than ₦500 per litre,” he said. ₦70,000 wage buys only 50 litres of petrol — JAF Rashidat Adesina of the Joint Action Front said the increase in petrol prices since the announcement of subsidy removal in 2023 had placed a disproportionate burden on low-income earners. She recalled that petrol sold for approximately ₦165 per litre before the subsidy was removed, after which the price rose to about ₦500 and subsequently ₦600 per litre. “We are now discussing prices of ₦1,350 to ₦1,400 per litre, depending on the location and filling station,” she said. Adesina challenged Nigerians to consider what the increase meant for workers whose monthly earnings remained far below the cost of maintaining a household. “What does this mean for workers and poor Nigerians?” she asked. She illustrated the situation by comparing the minimum wage with prevailing petrol prices, noting that a worker earning ₦70,000 monthly could purchase only 50 litres of petrol at ₦1,400 per litre. “The national minimum wage is ₦70,000 per month. At ₦1,400 per litre, an entire month’s minimum wage can purchase only 50 litres of petrol. That calculation does not include rent, school fees, food, transportation or other essential expenses,” she said. Adesina said the comparison demonstrated how rising energy costs had undermined workers’ ability to meet their basic needs, even before accounting for other household expenses. She also cited figures attributed to the National Bureau of Statistics that reportedly placed the national poverty threshold at approximately ₦345 per person per day, arguing that the figures reflected the vulnerability of households struggling with rising prices and stagnant incomes. However, the specific figures and their reference periods were not established in the address. “The consequences for ordinary Nigerians are severe. While workers and poor households struggle, sections of the business community continue to accumulate enormous wealth,” she said. Her remarks reinforced the central argument at the symposium that the burden of economic adjustment was falling disproportionately on workers, traders, artisans, young people and other low-income groups. Activists demand change in economic priorities The speakers called on the Federal Government to review economic policies they said had increased the cost of living without providing adequate protection for vulnerable citizens. They argued that reducing petrol prices, reviewing the minimum wage, stabilising the naira and investing in domestic refining should form part of a broader response to the economic crisis. items.title: Man United’s winless run extends to six games after Leeds draw
items.description: Manchester United’s winless run extended to six games after Leeds United held Michael Carrick’s side to a 1-1 draw in the Premier League at Elland Road on Sunday. Bryan Mbeumo gave Manchester United the lead in the 35th minute before Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised for Leeds shortly after the restart. The result leaves Manchester United 13th in the Premier League table, while Leeds sit seventh, three points ahead of their opponents. United took the lead when Mbeumo battled past James Justin to connect with a pass from Youri Tielemans and beat the Leeds defence 10 minutes before half-time. The visitors had earlier missed a chance to take the lead when Mbeumo headed wide from close range, while Leeds goalkeeper Senne Lammens produced a full-stretch save to deny Nico Elvedi. Leeds responded in the 51st minute as Calvert-Lewin beat Mbeumo to a loose ball following a corner, finishing after Tarik Muharemovic had made the initial contact. Both teams searched for a winner, but neither could find the decisive goal. Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes fired wide, while Leeds midfielder Anton Stach failed to keep his first-time effort on target. The draw extends United’s winless run in all competitions to six matches, their longest such streak since the end of the 2018-19 season. The result also denied Carrick a much-needed victory following a difficult week for the club, which included defender Lisandro Martinez being fined after criticising the club’s hierarchy. Martinez started against Leeds in a tense encounter that saw both Fernandes and Gabriel Gudmundsson booked during a fiery opening period. Leeds, meanwhile, maintained their unbeaten home record in all competitions since March. The Yorkshire club had beaten Manchester United 2-1 at Old Trafford in April, ending a 10-game winless run against their rivals in the Premier League, but were unable to repeat that result at Elland Road. items.title: Ghana Tourism Federation demands compensation for 85 businesses demolished at La Pleasure Beach
items.description: The Ghana Tourism Federation (GHATOF) is demanding compensation for 85 businesses affected by the demolition at La Pleasure Beach, warning that about 4,000 jobs, largely held by women, have been put at risk. The federation is also calling for the displaced traders to be given the first right of refusal in any future redevelopment of the beachfront, arguing that businesses operating with official permits should have received proper notice before their structures were demolished. At a meeting with affected traders on Wednesday, October 15, GHATOF said many of the businesses had operated at the beach for decades, contributing to the local economy through taxes, tourism levies and other statutory payments. The federation is seeking accountability from the district assemblies and public institutions that issued operating permits to some of the affected businesses. GHATOF President Seth Ocran said the federation would pursue compensation for the traders and advocate for their inclusion in plans for the future of the beachfront. He warned that demolishing businesses that had obtained official permits could undermine investor confidence in Ghana’s tourism sector. The demolition has particularly affected women involved in food vending, general trading and the sale of arts and crafts. Some traders say they have lost their main sources of income, along with equipment and other investments made in preparation for the December festive season, a peak period for tourism-related businesses. GHATOF argues that the consequences extend beyond the destruction of business structures, threatening livelihoods and employment linked to commercial activity at the beachfront. The federation says the affected businesses should be given the first right of refusal if commercial activities resume after redevelopment. The proposal is intended to give displaced traders an opportunity to return to the beachfront rather than be excluded from future business opportunities at the site. The dispute has also raised questions about the protection available to businesses operating under permits issued by public institutions and the responsibilities of authorities when such businesses are displaced. GHATOF says it will continue pressing for compensation and meaningful engagement with the affected traders as authorities consider the future of La Pleasure Beach. The federation maintains that how the matter is handled will have implications for the livelihoods of the displaced traders and confidence in Ghana’s tourism investment environment.

items.title: L’Algérie a atteint «l’autosuffisance dans la majorité des produits de l’industrie agroalimentaire», selon son ministre du Commerce
items.description: Apres avoir supervise l'ouverture de la Foire des produits agroalimentaires « Made in Algeria », le 17 octobre a Blida (ville situee a une cinquantaine de kilometres de la capitale Alger), organisee sous le theme « Qualite locale et perspectives prometteuses pour l'exportation », le ministre algerien du Commerce exterieur et de la Promotion des exportations, Kamel Rezig, a declare a la presse, en marge de l'evenement que « l'Algerie est parvenue a atteindre l'autosuffisance dans la majorite des produits de l'industrie agroalimentaire ». Accompagne de plusieurs ambassadeurs, charges d'affaires et cadres diplomatiques et economiques representant une vingtaine de pays, dont l'Arabie saoudite, la Jordanie, l'egypte, le Yemen, l'Italie, la Bulgarie, la Norvege, le Mali, le Bresil et la Chine, le ministre a souligne que l'Algerie a reussi « un bond en avant considerable dans le domaine de l'industrie agroalimentaire depuis 2020 », en fabriquant desormais localement « un grand nombre de produits » qui etaient auparavant importes. Vers la conquete des marches exterieurs De nombreuses entreprises algeriennes d'agroalimentaire s'orientent a present vers l'exportation et la conquete des marches exterieurs, a indique Kamel Rezig, dans une demarche soutenue et coordonnee entre le ministere et le gouvernement. Cette ambition est soutenue par la bonne qualite des produits algeriens, dont nombre d'entre eux ont reussi, grâce au respect des normes de qualite, a se placer dans les marches europeens, africains et arabes, a-t-il precise. La presence des delegations diplomatiques a cette foire s'inscrit aussi, selon les organisateurs, dans les efforts pour donner un elan aux produits algeriens sur les marches internationaux, en faisant connaître les productions agroalimentaires aux importateurs potentiels, en ouvrant dans la foulee de nouvelles opportunites de partenariats et de nouveaux debouches d'exportations. La foire des produits agroalimentaires devrait se poursuivre jusqu'au 20 octobre, avec la participation d'une centaine d'entreprises publiques et privees specialisees dans les divers secteurs de la production alimentaire.

items.title: Cairo vows support for Riyadh as 2 Saudi officers killed in helicopter crash near Yemen
items.description: Egypt is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security and stability, the presidency said on Sunday. Earlier in the day, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said two officers were killed when their helicopter crashed near the Yemen border, after the rebel group claimed it shot the aircraft down. The coalition blamed a “technical malfunction” for the helicopter crash, which inflicted its first military fatalities since the long-running conflict with the Houthis reignited in July. The incident comes a week after strikes by the Houthis killed 13 people at Riyadh’s international airport, the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade. An AH-6i reconnaissance helicopter belonging to the Saudi Ministry of National Guard crashed “inside Saudi territory in Najran Region due to a technical malfunction”, coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said, according to the official Saudi Press Agency . “The accident resulted in the martyrdom of its aircrew, consisting of two officers.” Late on Saturday, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed the group had “downed an Apache helicopter belonging to the Saudi enemy” in the same area. Egypt ready to give ‘all necessary and possible forms of support’ Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi had requested an urgent parliament session to authorise the military, one of the region’s largest and most powerful, to help defend Saudi Arabia if the kingdom requested its support. “Egypt will provide Saudi Arabia with all necessary and possible forms of support to defend its security and stability, protect its resources, territorial integrity and Islamic holy sites,” the Egyptian presidency said in a statement on Sunday. It followed a meeting of Egypt’s National Defence Council chaired by Sisi and attended by the parliamentary speaker, the prime minister and the army chief. A parliamentary vote had been expected on authorising the request for military support on Sunday, but discussions were due to continue on Monday, two lawmakers and local media reports said. Sisi said in a speech on Saturday that Egypt would act in accordance with guidance from Saudi King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, who visited Sisi on Sept 15, after fighting in Yemen reignited. Dar, Egypt FM condemn Houthi attacks On the diplomatic front, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar held a telephone conversation with Egypt’s FM Dr Badr Abdelatty, the Foreign Office (FO) said. “The two leaders exchanged views on recent regional developments and strongly condemned the Houthi attacks against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, reaffirming their full solidarity with the Kingdom and support for its sovereignty, territorial integrity and security.” They also discussed cooperation under the R-4 (Pakistan, Egypt, Türkiye and Saudi Arabia) framework and looked forward to the next meeting of the R-4 soon to further strengthen mutual ties and to coordinate on the regional issues, the statement added. The foreign ministers of the four countries last met on Sept 21 in New York, where they had reaffirmed their support for Riyadh’s sovereignty and supported its right to self-defence. Pakistan, which has signed two defence agreements with Riyadh, has repeatedly expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia. The first one, the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement (SMDA), was signed in Sept 2025, under which the two countries pledged that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both. The two countries are also parties to the Makkah Defence Alliance, which also includes Turkiye. The pact was signed on August 7 and provides that an attack on one member state would be treated as an attack on all. Yemen fighting After an uneasy, four-year truce, Yemen’s conflict has surged back to life, with the Houthis declaring a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia in July. The conflict intensified when Houthis captured territory around the Bab al-Mandeb strait, the Red Sea chokepoint and vital export route for Saudi oil since Iran blockaded the Gulf’s Strait of Hormuz. The Houthis have also hit Saudi targets including tankers in the Red Sea , oil facilities and Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport . On the other hand, the Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government has launched repeated air raids on Houthi territory. The coalition said overnight that it intercepted two drones in the Riyadh area and a third over the oil-rich Eastern Province. Saudi authorities had earlier issued a threat alert in the capital. Two ballistic missiles “launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Khamis Mushait” were intercepted in the kingdom’s south, the coalition added. On Saturday, the Houthis reported that Saudi strikes killed 12 people in Yemen, including three children.

items.title: Liberia’s Vice President Jeremiah Koung arrives in Ghana for Mining in Motion Summit 2026

items.title: 5 football competitions Nigeria will miss in 2027 after qualification failures
items.description: Nigeria is set to miss five major international football competitions in 2027 after qualification setbacks involving the Super Falcons, Flying Eagles and Golden Eaglets. The setbacks affect both the men’s youth teams and the senior women’s national team, with Nigeria failing to secure places at the FIFA Women’s World Cup, the U-20 Africa Cup of Nations and the FIFA U-20 World Cup, among other tournaments. The Golden Eaglets’ elimination from the 2026 WAFU-B U-17 Championship following a 1-1 draw with Côte d’Ivoire on Saturday also ended their hopes of featuring at the 2027 U-17 Africa Cup of Nations and the FIFA U-17 World Cup. Here are five major competitions Nigeria will miss in 2027. 1. FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 Nigeria’s senior women’s national team, the Super Falcons, will miss the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil after failing to secure qualification through the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations campaign and subsequent qualification playoffs. The development is a setback for the nine-time African champions, who had hoped to return to the global tournament after reaching the round of 16 at the 2023 edition in Australia and New Zealand. 2. U-20 Africa Cup of Nations 2027 Nigeria’s Flying Eagles will miss the 2027 U-20 Africa Cup of Nations after failing to secure qualification through the WAFU-B regional tournament. The team lost 4-1 to Burkina Faso in the WAFU-B U-20 Championship final in August, with Burkina Faso earning qualification alongside tournament hosts Ghana. The absence will deny Nigeria another opportunity to compete for the continental title and secure a place at the global youth tournament. 3. FIFA U-20 World Cup 2027 The Flying Eagles’ failure to qualify for the U-20 Africa Cup of Nations also means Nigeria will miss the 2027 FIFA U-20 World Cup. The continental tournament serves as the qualification route for African teams seeking places at the global competition. Nigeria, a two-time runner-up at the FIFA U-20 World Cup, will therefore be absent from the next edition after failing to progress through the regional qualification process. 4. U-17 Africa Cup of Nations 2027 The Golden Eaglets will also miss the 2027 U-17 Africa Cup of Nations after their elimination from the 2026 WAFU-B U-17 Championship in Burkina Faso. Nigeria needed a victory against Côte d’Ivoire on Saturday to keep their qualification hopes alive but settled for a 1-1 draw. The result followed an opening defeat to Niger Republic, leaving the Nigerian side unable to advance to the semi-finals. The elimination extends Nigeria’s absence from the continental U-17 tournament, having also missed the previous two editions. 5. FIFA U-17 World Cup 2027 Nigeria’s failure to qualify for the U-17 Africa Cup of Nations also ends the Golden Eaglets’ hopes of featuring at the 2027 FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar. The country has won the competition five times, making it the most successful nation in the tournament’s history. However, the latest regional qualification setback means the team will miss another edition of the global competition. The Golden Eaglets last participated in 2019, when they reached the round of 16 in Brazil. The absence of the three national teams from these competitions represents a difficult period for Nigerian football, particularly at youth level, where the country has historically enjoyed considerable success. items.title: Automobile : la Chine détrône l’Europe en Algérie, plus de 190.000 véhicules importés en 8 mois
items.description: La Chine est devenue le principal pays de provenance des véhicules importés en Algérie, détrônant ainsi l’Europe qui a longtemps occupé cette place avec les constructeurs français Renault et Peugeot et l’allemand Volkswagen. Un premier chiffre concernant le volume de ces importations , faites essentiellement par des particuliers, vient d'être dévoilé : plus de 190 000 unités en huit mois contre 140 000 durant le premier semestre 2026. Il a été livré par un média sud-coréen, citant les données d'une association professionnelle et des douanes chinoises. Exportations chinoises de véhicules : l'Algérie dans le top 10 Le site coréen Asia Economy rapporte que les exportations automobiles de Chine s'étendent rapidement au-delà de la Russie et de l'Amérique latine pour conquérir les marchés développés, notamment l'Europe et l'Australie. L’Algérie figure dans le top 10 des plus grands importateurs de véhicules de Chine. “ Cette offensive commerciale, qui mise sur la compétitivité des prix et les technologies d'électrification, semble bouleverser la donne concurrentielle sur le marché automobile traditionnel ”, estime le média. L’Association chinoise de la distribution automobile prévoit que les exportations de véhicules du pays atteindront cette année environ 12 millions d'unités, contre 8,32 millions en 2025, indique Asia Economy. L’Algérie a importé 190 000 véhicules de Chine entre janvier et août 2026 Entre janvier et août de cette année, ces exportations se sont élevées à 7,45 millions d’unités, en hausse de 51 % par rapport à la même période de l'année dernière, ont révélé pour leur part les douanes chinoises, citées par le même média. Les exportations du seul mois d'août ont dépassé le million d'unités. Le premier pays acheteur de véhicules chinois est la Russie avec 638 000 unités pendant la même période de 2026. La Russie est suivie par le Brésil (480 000 véhicules), le Royaume-Uni (365 000), l'Australie (326 000), la Belgique (322 000) et le Mexique (320 844). L'Europe à la traîne Les autres clients de la Chine sont les Philippines qui ont importé 214 000 véhicules chinois pendant la même période, l’Italie (209 000), et les Émirats arabes unis (196 000). L'Algérie arrive en dixième position avec 190 045 véhicules importés de Chine entre janvier et août 2026. L’Empire du milieu détrône l’Europe qui a longtemps dominé le marché algérien de l’automobile avec les constructeurs français, Renault et Peugeot, et l’Allemand Volkswagen. Renault ne vend plus de voitures en Algérie et son usine locale est toujours fermée. Même situation pour le groupe Volkswagen. Pour Peugeot, il ne vend plus lui aussi de voitures en Algérie depuis 2020. Le seul constructeur présent en Algérie est Stellantis dont fait partie le groupe français PSA (Peugeot-Citroën); mais c'est la marque Fiat qui a ouvert une usine d'assemblage de véhicules à Oran en décembre 2023. Pour les importations opérées par les particuliers, ces derniers préfèrent désormais la Chine en raison des prix des voitures plus abordables qu’en Europe et les facilités d’obtention du visa. L’article Automobile : la Chine détrône l’Europe en Algérie, plus de 190.000 véhicules importés en 8 mois est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 'Like we had a war': Over 1,800 arrested as France counts cost of violent protests
items.description: France was reeling on Sunday from widespread damage caused by violent protests the day before that saw 1,800 people arrested, a historic town hall torched and widespread looting. “It’s like we had a war,” a 78-year-old resident in central Paris, Mehmet Ozeden, told AFP amid burnt street barricades from the protests. The convulsion raised the stakes for French President Emmanuel Macron, who is in his final months in power before elections to replace him in six months’ time. It followed weeks of student protests that had also turned violent at times. Macron was to address the nation Sunday evening at 1800 GMT, his office said, after meeting key ministers. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 1,800 people were arrested over the protests and looting, with investigations under way “to identify the perpetrators of these acts so they can be brought to justice”. Torched cars, smashed shopfronts and burnt debris scarred numerous streets in Paris, where officials said 557 people were in custody after a “record” number of arrests. The capital experienced “a level of violence that we have never, I believe, seen before”, said Paris deputy mayor Lamia El Aaraje. Hundreds of shops were looted in Paris and other cities, including Marseille, Bordeaux, Nice and Strasbourg, during the protests over the cost of living . One person died during the main march in Paris, but officials said it was health-related and not linked to the protest violence. Around 1,500 businesses were damaged, causing losses estimated in the hundreds of millions of euros, according to the Retail and Trade Federation. One Paris resident, Anita Gras, out for a jog between the debris, said she saw young men loot a sports shoe retailer. “They stayed until 1:00 am, we were afraid they were going to throw things at us,” she said. “It’s appalling, terrifying — groups of young people came here yesterday (Saturday), looting, smashing everything, with total impunity,” said another resident, 57-year-old Cecile Rogue, surveying a pile of charred bicycles. A pedestrian runs past damages and a broken frontage windows of a shop a day after riot and looting following a nationwide protest against the “high cost of living”, in Lyon central-eastern France on October 18, 2026. — AFP ‘Wild horde’ The city of Limoges lost its 19th-century town hall to a fire. The local prefect, Maurice Barate, told news channel LCI it had been deliberately set by “a wild horde” and was only brought under control early on Sunday. The mayor of Lyon, Gregory Doucet, said “the chaos that reigned in the city for several hours was abominable”. A tourist office in the centre of Lyon was set ablaze during the protests, which saw multiple clashes and looting. Political recriminations have followed, with the government and far-right leader Marine Le Pen blaming ultra-left groups, while far-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon accused authorities of inflaming tensions. Paris’s Socialist deputy mayor El Aaraje accused Le Pen’s party of “acting like a pyromaniac firefighter”, using the protests to further her presidential ambitions. French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu was to chair a crisis meeting of ministers at 0800 GMT on Monday, his office said. They were to look at the insurance and help for impacted shops as well as the prosecution of perpetrators of the violence. Half a million demonstrators In Paris, startled tourists were seen on Saturday running with suitcases along streets filled with tear gas and protesters. A Danish tourist, Soren Petersen, said it was “sad” to see damage to Paris buildings. “It is not a protest, it’s far beyond a normal protest,” he told AFP . An American tourist, Jill Burns, said “we were scared”. Around 500 police, firefighters and paramedics were hurt in the protests, the interior minister said. The violence took place on the sidelines of nationwide protests that the interior ministry said were attended by 550,000 people. The CGT union said 800,000 people participated. A woman stands next to a damaged Micromania-Zing video game retail shop at Jean-Medecin avenue in Nice, southeastern France on October 18, 2026, after a nationwide protests against the “high cost of living”. — AFP A 17-year-old boy had his right hand blown off by a crowd-control grenade in the southern city of Saint-Etienne. Analyst Mujtaba Rahman of the Eurasia Group think tank said on X that most of the demonstrations on Saturday were peaceful, and “the violence came from a fringe of the ultra left” with looting “by opportunistic gangs from the poor suburbs”. “All good news for Marine Le Pen,” he said. France’s Yellow Vest movement , which staged street protests eight years ago against Macron’s government over planned fuel-tax hikes, had called Saturday’s “yellow and youth” demonstrations. The principal grievance was the cost of living, pushed up in part by the war in the Middle East, which has helped send inflation soaring in Europe as elsewhere. Trump says country ‘shattered’ by immigration US President Donald Trump, meanwhile, blamed immigration for unrest during protests in France and urged the country to tighten its migration rules. “France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country,” Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform. “Close your Borders and take control, before it is too late!” Trump’s post comes after similar comments made by US Vice President JD Vance on Saturday. “Western liberals imported the third world into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion. They ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility. They were told it would lead to this and they didn’t listen,” Vance wrote on X . “I pray that France, a beautiful country of amazing people, will stop this madness before more of its landmarks burn,” he added. Vance, who is seen as a potential presidential candidate in the 2028 election, also drew a connection to upcoming midterm races for congressional seats on November 3, where Republicans are not expected to perform well.

items.title: Ashaiman police demolish suspected criminal hideouts at Fitter-Line
items.description: The Ashaiman District Police Command has demolished structures identified as suspected criminal hideouts at Fitter-Line following a swoop aimed at curbing criminal activities in the area ahead of the Christmas festivities. The operation, conducted at about 6:40 a.m. on Saturday, October 17, was led by District Commander DSP Orlando Joseph Adzokpa and involved 30 police personnel. According to the police, the exercise targeted suspected criminals believed to be terrorising residents in and around Ashaiman, as part of efforts to dismantle hideouts and improve public safety. The suspects reportedly fled upon seeing the police team approaching, leaving officers with no arrests to make. The team, however, demolished the structures identified as hideouts during the operation. The exercise ended at about 8:40 a.m. without any incident. The command said the operation would continue as part of measures to combat crime and enable residents to go about their daily activities and conduct legitimate businesses without fear or intimidation before, during and after the Christmas season.

items.title: Rural telephony to see a boost in connectivity
items.description: The Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations has promised improved telecommunications connectivity across the country following an infrastructure expansion project. The sector minister, Sam Nortey George, indicated that about 2,016 mini telecommunication masts are being constructed, with 5,000 more communities to be covered to achieve complete nationwide coverage. He said this during an inspection exercise in the Volta Region, where he led teams from the Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations and the Ghana Investment Fund for Electronic Communication (GIFEC) to inspects construction of the rural telephony sites, intended to improve access to telecommunication services. Mr Nartey was dissatisfied with the progress of construction at some of the sites, although about 1,600 of the rural telephony sites have been completed, and issued a 30-day ultimatum to contractors yet to complete their sites, warning that they would be surcharged for the extra time taken to complete the project. “When it comes to rural telephony sites, we are supposed to do about 2,016 of them; currently we have more than 1,600 that we are told have been completed, 1,400 are active and are passing traffic at the moment”. “As I said, on Tuesday, we are having this meeting to do a reconciliation; like I said 30 days from Tuesday, we will begin to surcharge the contracts. We still have close to 5,000 communities that we need to cover”, he explained. Mr Nortey further indicated plans to upgrade the existing networks to 4G to enhance telecommunications service delivery across the country. He expressed hope that the Finance Ministry would continue to make funds available for the expansion and upgrading projects. “I have been speaking not just about expanding the network but upgrading the existing networks because the sites that are coming up are 2G and 3G and I believe that we must upgrade all of them to 4G”, he said. Fibre cuts dwindle efforts to enhance telecommunication connectivity Mr Nortey, however, lamented that about 4,000 fibre cuts were recorded between January and June 2026, undermining efforts to improve the country’s telecommunications network. He explained that damaged fibre-optic network cables lose about 4% of their quality upon restoration, and called for better coordination between his ministry and road contractors to prevent frequent cuts. “It’s engineering; it’s pure physics, if you cut fibre and you fix the fibre, it loses some quality. It’s a ring, so once you cut the ring every site on that ring gets taken off or gets a degradation in its quality of service”, he explained. He further indicated that “we love the roads, we want the roads to be done but we need to coordinate it in a way that the construction of the roads doesn’t affect us. But the road construction is not the only reason; galamaey is another one”, he revealed. Traditional authorities lauded the Ministry for the service expansion drive, hoping it would help transform their livelihoods. “This installation is more than just hardware; it is a bridge to the rest of the world. It provides our youth with the digital connectivity necessary to drive the modern era. Your commitment to bringing the telephony site to our doorsteps is a transformative gift that will change lives right here in our town”, said Togbe Dikro of Akofe Gadza. One Million Coders Programme Mr Nartey also visited One Coders Programme training centres in Ho, Kpetoe, Adaklu Waya and the University of Health and Allied Sciences. He was enthused by the level of cooperation and enthusiasm shown by trainees at the various centres. He encouraged the trainees to recognise the initiative as life-changing and to endeavour to complete all stages of the training, which currently has a 91% completion rate. The Communications Ministry also equipped the training centre at the University of Health and Allied Sciences with about 100 laptops to enable students to acquire practical digital and networking skills.

items.title: Gov’t publishes names of 1,964 Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa
items.description: The government spent GH¢49.72 million to evacuate 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa following a resurgence of xenophobic attacks, Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has disclosed. Speaking at a media briefing on Monday, September 7, 2026, Mr Ablakwa said the evacuation exercise, which began on May 27 and ended on September 4, was undertaken to protect Ghanaians amid growing threats, intimidation and violence against foreign nationals. He said the government spent GH¢33.72 million on the operation, while Engineers and Planners, owned by businessman Ibrahim Mahama, contributed GH¢16 million towards the total cost. The expenditure covered chartered flights and tickets, ground transportation, feeding, accommodation, medical care, reintegration support and the repatriation of the remains of two deceased Ghanaians. Mr Ablakwa said each returnee received GH¢5,000 as a reintegration grant and GH¢500 as a travel and transport allowance. Additional assistance included free medical screening, National Health Insurance Scheme registration, food packages, SIM cards loaded with data and airtime, psychosocial support and accommodation provided by partner organisations. The minister said the government had also enrolled the returnees in a special national database to facilitate access to employment, entrepreneurship support, skills development and start-up opportunities. Four Ghanaians die amid xenophobic violence Mr Ablakwa disclosed that four Ghanaians died in connection with the reported violence and difficult circumstances surrounding the attacks in South Africa. They were Bashiru Issahaq, 44, who was killed in Khayelitsha, Cape Town, on June 30; Kwadwo Antwi, who was murdered in Prieska on July 18; Amoonu Jailor Nash, who was killed in East London on April 3; and Ebenezer Ayi Tawiah, who died upon arrival at the Accra International Airport on August 17 after reportedly being unable to access medical care amid harassment. The minister said the government, through Ghana’s High Commission in Pretoria, had engaged South African authorities to pursue investigations and ensure that those responsible for the deaths were brought to justice. He added that the government had formally protested the attacks and raised concerns with South African officials over the safety of Ghanaian nationals. Ghana petitions African Union Mr Ablakwa said Ghana had also petitioned the African Union Commission on May 6 to place xenophobic attacks against African nationals in South Africa on the continental agenda. He said the petition had received the unanimous endorsement of the ECOWAS Authority of Heads of State and Government and that the African Union Commission had indicated that the matter would be discussed at the AU Summit expected in January 2027. The minister said the government remained committed to addressing the root causes of xenophobic violence and protecting the rights and dignity of Ghanaian citizens abroad. Government invites Auditor-General to audit evacuations As part of its transparency and accountability measures, the Foreign Affairs Ministry said it had made public the names of evacuees, ticket receipts and other relevant documents relating to the operation. The government also invited the Auditor-General to conduct an audit of all evacuation exercises undertaken since 2017. Mr Ablakwa said the evacuation was voluntary and aimed at protecting Ghanaians facing distressing circumstances in South Africa, adding that the government considered the protection of citizens’ lives and dignity more important than the financial cost. He further announced plans to establish a Ghanaian Diaspora Consular Fund to provide emergency assistance to Ghanaians facing crises anywhere in the world. The minister reaffirmed the government’s commitment to transparency, accountability and the welfare of Ghanaians abroad.

items.title: Bataille de Kiidga : Boussouma honore la mémoire de ceux qui ont résisté à l’occupation française
items.description: À l’occasion de la commémoration du 130ᵉ anniversaire des batailles d’octobre 1896 dans le Riungu de Boussouma, le ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo, a effectué une visite sur le site historique de Kiidga, ce dimanche 18 octobre 2026 à Boussouma. Cette commémoration vise à rendre hommage aux résistants qui se sont opposés à l’occupation coloniale française menée par les lieutenants Voulet et Chanoine, notamment lors de la bataille de Kiidga, au sud de Mané, le 18 octobre 1896. La résistance à l'occupation fut entreprise à la rivière située au sud de Mané a Kiidiga, le 18 octobre 1896 notamment par l'intrépide armée des Yarcés du canton de Mané conduite par Yarnaaba Zombãnega. Malgré les pertes importantes dans leurs rangs, les guerriers refusèrent la fuite et affrontèrent courageusement la mort. Beaucoup furent décapités devant leurs femmes et enfants médusés et leurs cadavres mélangés à ceux d'animaux que les colons préparèrent dans de grandes jarres pour donner à manger aux rescapés et autres prisonniers qu'ils firent. Mané fut totalement incendiée et aucun grenier ne fut épargné pour accentuer la famine. Il y eut beaucoup de martyrs dont les plus célèbres sont : Gnoudou de Googhin, Malik Kebré, Boureima de Bullin et Baba de Pampanghin avec des exploits surhumains. Gnoudou par exemple se fit enchaîné par ses partisans à un gros arbre avec son tas de flèches à côté parce qu'il dit que « les pieds peuvent aller souvent là où la tête ne souhaite pas ». Il y fit plusieurs victimes parmi les assaillants français et aucun fusil ne percuta sur lui. Pour le tuer, il a fallu le crucifier et poser de grosses pierres sur sa poitrine! items.title: Tinubu has achieved more for Nigeria than predecessors in 16 years — Dafinone
items.description: *Rallies 250 Urhobo Communities for APC Ahead of 2027 Senator Ede Dafinone, representing Delta Central Senatorial District, has declared that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has done more to fix Nigeria than previous presidents in the past 16 years, arguing that the administration’s tough economic policies are necessary to reverse decades of national challenges and reposition the country for sustainable growth. Dafinone made the assertion on Saturday at Wetland Hotel, Ughelli, Delta State, during a consultation meeting with community youth leaders drawn from 250 communities in Ughelli South and Udu Local Government Areas, where he rallied support for the All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Delta Central lawmaker maintained that President Tinubu had demonstrated the political courage to confront longstanding national challenges, stressing that although some of his policies appear tough and have brought hardship to Nigerians, they are necessary to reposition the country for economic recovery and lasting prosperity. He expressed confidence that the difficult decisions being taken by the administration would ultimately yield positive results, urging Nigerians to remain patient as the government works towards stabilising the economy and improving living conditions. Turning to the 2027 general elections, Dafinone commended President Tinubu and Delta State Governor, Rt. Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori, for what he described as their commendable performance, stressing the importance of continuity and political cooperation in sustaining development. He argued that both leaders were delivering on their responsibilities and that the principle of not changing a winning team should guide political considerations ahead of the elections. The senator urged youth leaders from the 250 communities to support APC candidates across all levels, including the presidency, governorship, Senate, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly. According to him, political alignment between the Federal Government, Delta State Government and elected representatives would strengthen opportunities for attracting infrastructure projects, employment initiatives and other developmental interventions to Urhobo communities. Dafinone cautioned against dissipating political support on opposition parties, arguing that the Urhobo Nation stood to benefit more from effective representation and cooperation with the governments at the federal and state levels. Speaking on his re-election ambition, the senator assured the people of Ughelli South, Ughelli North and Udu Federal Constituency that his experience and growing influence in the National Assembly would enhance his ability to attract more dividends of democracy to the area. He maintained that returning him to the Senate as a ranking lawmaker, with the backing of President Tinubu and Governor Oborevwori, would strengthen his capacity to facilitate federal projects, youth empowerment programmes and other interventions across Delta Central. Dafinone reaffirmed his commitment to effective representation, stressing that in all his decisions, Urhobo comes first and will never allow Urhobo to be shortchanged, and the development of the Urhobo Nation is paramount to him, assuring constituents that their interests would remain central to his legislative priorities. He urged the youth leaders to remain united and actively engaged in the political process, describing grassroots participation as essential to achieving the development aspirations of Delta Central ahead of the 2027 general elections. He also tasked the youth leaders to ignore lies told by his opponent about him fighting to relocate projects sighted out of Urhobo, stressing that he is a well-brought-up Urhobo son, and that Urhobo blood flows in his veins. According to him, “My father worked and fought for the Urhobo Nation, and he brought me up very well. Urhobo blood flows through my veins, so how is it possible for me to relocate a project in Orogun, Urhoboland, to another place? Please ignore lies told by my opponents who believe that politics is all about propaganda.” Speaking also, the member representing Ughelli North, South and Udu federal constituency, Rt. Hon. Francis Waive, charged the community youth leaders to continue to support the APC, noting that another person coming to tell them stories will bring suffering to their community as APC and Tinubu will win the next elections. Waive noted that as an opposition lawmaker you have just few privileges, urging Urhobo Nation not to fall for the deceit of voting for another party outside APC come 2027, “As an opposition lawmaker at the national level, you cannot do much if you’re not on the side of the President, so, don’t be deceived, APC will serve Urhobo best interest. Notable APC leaders at the event, include Chief Paulinus Akpeki; Chief Adelabu Bodjor; Hon. Austine Ayemidejor; former Sapele Local Government Chairman, Chief Eugene Inoaghan; APC candidate for Sapele State Constituency II, Hon. Ejiro Jamani; and other party leaders. items.title: Playback: The Law examined enforcement of laws on teacher sexual abuse
items.description: This Sunday’s edition of JoyNews’ The Law examined the enforcement of laws on teacher sexual abuse in the country. The programme, hosted by Samson Anyenini, explored the legal framework for protecting students from sexual abuse, the accountability of teachers accused of such offences, and the steps required to ensure justice for victims. Guests who joined the discussion are Marian Darlington, Executive Secretary and Head of Public Relations of the African Women Lawyers Association (AWLA), and Lady Rev. Amesika Apprey of A-Partners@Law. The programme comes amid growing public concern over the handling of sexual abuse allegations at Obuasi Senior High Technical School, where the headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, has been interdicted pending investigations into allegations involving female students. A JoyNews investigation by Manasseh Azure Awuni reported that complaints had allegedly been made to school management and education authorities months before the matter gained national attention, raising questions about institutional accountability and the protection of students. JoyNews Research has also documented at least 44 cases involving teachers and school heads accused of sexually abusing students between January 2015 and October 2026, with more than half having no reported verdict or final sanction. The discussion on The Law is expected to examine whether existing legal and administrative measures are sufficient to protect students, how complaints should be handled, and what steps are needed to ensure accountability when allegations of sexual abuse arise.

items.title: 52e session du Conseil des ministres des Affaires étrangères de l’OCI : les émissaires de la Confédération des États du Sahel harmonisent leurs positions
items.description: La République d'Irak abrite les 17 et 18 octobre 2026, les travaux de la 52e session du Conseil des ministres des Affaires étrangères de l'Organisation de coopération islamique (OCI). Placée sous le thème : « Dialogue et solidarité, deux piliers fondamentaux pour promouvoir la paix et le développement durable », cette session réunit les responsables de l'OCI et des Nations Unies, ainsi que les Chefs de la diplomatie des États membres de l'Organisation ou leurs représentants. L'ouverture des travaux a été présidée, ce samedi 17 octobre 2026 à Bagdad, par le Premier ministre de la République d'Irak, Son Excellence Monsieur Ali Faleh AL-ZAIDI. Le Burkina Faso est représenté à cette tribune de haut niveau par une délégation conduite par l’Ambassadeur du Burkina Faso auprès du Royaume d'Arabie saoudite, le camarade Boukary SAVADOGO. Il est accompagné de la Directrice générale de la Coopération multilatérale, la camarade Mariame FOFANA et du chef du service Coopération afro-arabe, le camarade Toussaint OUATTARA. En marge des travaux de la 52e session de l’OCI, les délégations du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger ont tenu une réunion de concertation afin d'harmoniser leurs vues et leurs actions pour mieux porter la voix de la Confédération des Etats du Sahel lors des travaux. Les échanges ont essentiellement porté sur les enjeux de la participation de la Confédération à cette session du Conseil des ministres des Affaires étrangères de l’OCI avec la ferme volonté de plaider en faveur du renforcement du Bureau régional de l'Organisation au Niger et de la prise en compte des résolutions de l'AES. Outre la question des candidatures abordée notamment sous l'angle de la convergence de vues du Groupe Africain de l'OCI, les échanges ont également porté sur la prochaine édition du FESPACO qui se tiendra du 27 février au 6 mars 2027, dans la capitale burkinabè. La rencontre des émissaires de la Confédération AES s’inscrit dans une dynamique de souveraineté visant à veiller à la prise en compte des priorités du Sahel et à consolider le partenariat avec l'OCI et ses Etats membres. DCRP/MAE

items.title: Trump links unrest in France to immigration, urges tougher rules
items.description: US President Donald Trump on Sunday blamed immigration for unrest during protests in France and urged the country to tighten its migration rules. “France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country,” Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform. “Close your Borders and take control, before it is too late!” France was reeling Sunday from widespread damage during protests the day before that left a historic town hall torched and led to 1,800 arrests, piling pressure on President Emmanuel Macron six months before elections to replace him. Trump’s post comes after similar comments made by Vice President JD Vance on Saturday. “Western liberals imported the third world into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion. They ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility. They were told it would lead to this and they didn’t listen,” Vance wrote on X. “I pray that France, a beautiful country of amazing people, will stop this madness before more of its landmarks burn,” he added. Vance, who is seen as a potential presidential candidate in the 2028 election, also drew a connection to upcoming midterm races for congressional seats on November 3, where Republicans are not expected to perform well. items.title: Élections au CSPJ : dix magistrats élus avec une participation de 94,9 %
items.description: Les magistrats ont largement participé au renouvellement de leurs représentants au sein du Conseil supérieur du pouvoir judiciaire (CSPJ). Organisées le samedi 17 octobre 2026, les élections ont enregistré un taux de participation de 94,9 % et abouti à l’élection de dix magistrats issus des cours d’appel et des tribunaux de première instance, selon les résultats définitifs annoncés par l’institution. Dans un communiqué, le Conseil précise que ces résultats ont été établis après le dépouillement des bulletins dans les bureaux de vote et la transmission des procès-verbaux à la commission centrale de recensement, chargée de consolider les résultats conformément aux dispositions légales et réglementaires en vigueur. Parmi les représentants des magistrats des cours d’appel, Hicham Bahar arrive en tête avec 631 voix, devant Abderrazak Jebari, qui en a obtenu 590, et Mustapha Aït Aïssa, crédité de 449 voix. Imane Msaïd se classe quatrième avec 310 voix. Dans le collège des magistrats des tribunaux de première instance, Abderrahmane Sebaï arrive en première position avec 1.549 voix. Il est suivi de Hicham Hadri, qui recueille 1.135 voix, et de Samir Aït Arjdal, avec 827 voix. Sahar Azzouzi obtient 692 voix, devant Nazim Lakhdar, qui en totalise 674. Souad Dada se classe sixième avec 613 voix. À l’issue du scrutin, le CSPJ a félicité les magistrates et magistrats élus, saluant la confiance accordée par leurs pairs. Il a également souligné le sens des responsabilités et la discipline ayant marqué le déroulement des opérations électorales, ainsi que la participation active des magistrats au choix de leurs représentants. L’institution a par ailleurs remercié les candidates et candidats, les présidents et membres des bureaux de vote, les commissions de recensement et l’ensemble des personnes ayant contribué à l’organisation du scrutin. Pour le Conseil, cette élection constitue une étape dans le renforcement de la représentation des magistrats en son sein et dans la consolidation de l’indépendance du pouvoir judiciaire. L’institution inscrit cette démarche dans le respect des principes constitutionnels et des valeurs éthiques et professionnelles de la magistrature. The post Élections au CSPJ : dix magistrats élus avec une participation de 94,9 % appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .
